items.abstract: <jats:p>Direct laser acceleration can generate high-current relativistic electron beams, yet their intrinsically large divergence severely limits beam transport and subsequent applications. In this work, a compact collimation scheme for direct-laser-accelerated electron beams is proposed and numerically investigated. By placing a wedge above the gas jet target, the gas flow is modified to form a millimeter-scale plasma region downstream of the jet, which acts as an integrated plasma lens for the accelerated electron beam. Numerical results show that, after passing through this plasma-lens region, the electron beam divergence can be reduced by approximately a factor of two. Owing to its simple configuration and ease of implementation, this scheme offers an effective route to improve the transport properties of electron beams without requiring complex target fabrication or stringent alignment. These results demonstrate that wedge-modified gas jet targets are promising for manipulating and applying electron beams in compact radiation sources and advanced accelerator systems.</jats:p>
title: Collimation of direct-laser-accelerated electron beams via a wedge-modified gas jet target

items.abstract: <jats:p>Wound healing is a complex, dynamic biological process that relies on the integration of cells, soluble mediators, the extracellular matrix, and an adequate blood supply. Systemic conditions, such as diabetes mellitus, vascular insufficiency, and chronic inflammatory states, can compromise this process and lead to wounds that are difficult to heal. In this context, photobiomodulation (PBM) has been widely studied as an adjunctive therapy. Specifically, Intravascular Laser Irradiation of Blood (ILIB) has attracted interest because of its potential systemic, rather than merely local, effects. This study aimed to analyze, through an integrative literature review, the available evidence on the use of ILIB and its photobiological foundations in the wound-healing process. The synthesis indicates that the proposed mechanisms of ILIB include the modulation of mitochondrial activity, nitric oxide release, reduction of oxidative stress, improvement of blood rheological parameters, and cytokine modulation. Although experimental and in vitro studies support the biological plausibility of these effects, the clinical literature specifically addressing ILIB and wound healing remains scarce, heterogeneous regarding dosimetric parameters, and largely of low methodological quality. It is concluded that ILIB is a biologically plausible and potentially promising adjunctive approach; however, randomized, controlled clinical trials with standardized protocols are required before firm recommendations can be established.</jats:p>
title: O uso do laser ILIB na cicatrização: uma revisão integrativa da literatura
The use of ILIB laser in wound healing: an integrative literature review

<jats:p>Abstract.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Adaptive finite elements combined with geometric multigrid solvers are one of the most efficient numerical methods for problems such as the instationary Navier–Stokes equations. Yet despite their efficiency, computations remain expensive and the simulation of, for example, complex flow problems can take many hours or days. GPUs provide an interesting avenue to speed up the calculations due to their very high theoretical performance. However, the large degree of parallelism and non-standard API make the use of GPUs in scientific computing challenging. In this work, we develop a GPU acceleration for the adaptive finite element library Gascoigne and study its effectiveness for different systems of partial differential equations. Our goal is thereby to integrate the GPU acceleration into the existing code with minimal changes. Through the systematic formulation of all computations as linear algebra operations, we can employ GPU-accelerated linear algebra libraries, which simplifies the implementation and ensures the maintainability of the code while achieving very efficient GPU utilizations. Our results for a transport-diffusion equation, linear elasticity, and the instationary Navier–Stokes equations show substantial speedups of up to 20X compared to multicore CPU implementations.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and data available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SISC and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15582537 . [Formula: see text]</jats:p>
title: An Adaptive Finite Element Multigrid Solver Using GPU Acceleration

<jats:sec id="sec001">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To explore the relationship between the GOLD biological age difference (GOLD BioAgeDiff)—a quantitative measure of aging—and urinary incontinence using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="sec002">
                    <jats:title>Materials and methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In NHANES, weighted multinomial logistic regression assessed UI subtypes, ordinal logistic regression assessed severity; additional analyses included propensity score matching (PSM), restricted cubic splines (RCSs), subgroup analyses, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). In CHARLS, Cox models and Kaplan-Meier curves evaluated incident UI.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="sec003">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>GOLD BioAgeDiff was associated with urge (OR 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01–1.04) and mixed UI (OR 1.02, 95% CI: 1.00–1.03), but not stress UI. Each 1-unit increase raised severe UI odds by 3% (OR 1.03); the highest quartile had 52% higher risk (OR 1.52). A nonlinear relationship was observed (P < 0.001); no interaction remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons in exploratory subgroup analyses. XGBoost ranked GOLD BioAgeDiff as a key predictor. In CHARLS, Light BioAgeDiff predicted incident UI (HR 1.01, 1.00–1.02).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="sec004">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>GOLD BioAgeDiff is significantly associated with UI severity, subtype, and incidence—especially for urge and mixed UI. As a quantifiable marker of biological aging, it may provide complementary information for risk stratification in population-based settings.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Biological age acceleration and urinary incontinence: A combined analysis from two national cohorts in the United States and China

items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Thulium fiber laser (TFL) has been proposed as an alternative to holmium:yttrium-aluminum-garnet (Ho:YAG) laser for endoscopic lithotripsy, but its incremental benefit over contemporary Ho:YAG systems remains uncertain.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to May 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing TFL with Ho:YAG laser lithotripsy for upper urinary tract stones were included. Continuous outcomes were pooled as mean differences (MDs), and dichotomous outcomes were pooled as odds ratios (ORs). Subgroup analyses were performed according to stone-free rate (SFR) definition, stone location, and use of Modulated Oscillating Pulse Energy System (MOSES) 2.0 technology. Additional exploratory analyses examined stone burden, imaging modality, surgical modality, and study initiation period.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Twelve RCTs involving 1383 patients were included. TFL was associated with shorter total operation time (MD = −6.65 minutes, 95% confidence interval [CI]: −9.52 to −3.79) and lasering time (MD = −3.92 minutes, 95% CI: −5.65 to −2.20). Complete SFR favored TFL (OR = 1.70, 95% CI: 1.13–2.54), whereas SFR allowing clinically insignificant residual fragments (CIRFs) did not (OR = 1.71, 95% CI: 0.86–3.37). Hospital stay, postoperative stenting, ureteral perforation, mucosal injury, and Clavien–Dindo grades I–III complications were comparable. In exploratory comparisons using MOSES 2.0, TFL showed no significant advantage in operation time or SFR.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>TFL appears to improve lithotripsy efficiency and complete stone clearance without increasing most complications. Its advantage is less clear when small residual fragments are accepted or when the comparator uses MOSES 2.0 technology.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Thulium Fiber Laser vs Ho:YAG Laser Lithotripsy for Upper Urinary Tract Stones: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

items.abstract: <jats:p>Laser doping is one of the routes available for forming a selective emitter on boron-diffused n-type silicon, but the power range within which the process is both dopant-effective and repairable had not been delimited. This work follows a laser-doped selective emitter from 30 to 40 W and asks what a subsequent oxidation can and cannot undo. Morphology, reflectance, sheet resistance and electrochemical capacitance-voltage profiles were taken at a fixed point of the fabrication sequence, and symmetric test structures were measured before and after the oxidation so that the repair step could be separated from the presence of the selective emitter. Between 30 and 35 W the oxidation recovers most of the recombination that the laser introduces and lowers the peak surface concentration to 8.4–9.1 × 1018 cm−3, a behavior consistent with boron segregation into the growing oxide and with the annealing of part of the laser-induced defects. At 40 W the pyramids collapse and ablation pits open, and the same oxidation partially repaired only about 14% of the saturation current density, against 40%–43% at the two lower powers. Cells printed with the 35 W emitter reach an average efficiency of 25.60% against 25.26% for the homogeneous reference.</jats:p>
title: Laser-Power-Dependent Damage and Post-Oxidation Repair in Laser-Doped Selective Emitters for High-Efficiency TOPCon Solar Cells

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Grid components have a significant impact on the performance of radio-frequency (RF) ion thruster. Based on the theoretical analysis of the ionization and acceleration process of the RF ion thruster (RIT), it is found that the grid position of the RIT may affect the RF power distribution, and the grid structure may affect the process of electron energy acquisition in the skin layer, and then affect the ionization of the working medium, then indirectly affect the acceleration process. In this paper, the discharge performance and beam extraction performance of thruster with different grid axial positions and distribution of holes are compared by experiments. The experimental results show that the axial position of the grid will affect the eddy current loss of the grid, and thus affect the power distribution. The difference of the opening area of the grid has no significant effect on the power distribution, but it will significantly affect the extraction performance of the thruster. The coupling effects between ionization and acceleration process is analyzed in this paper, which can provide guidance for the design of grid position and structural parameters of miniature RIT.</jats:p>
title: Grid position and structure effects on ionization-acceleration in RF thruster

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to evaluate the physicochemical characteristics, reactive species, storage stability, and antimicrobial activity of plasma-activated water (PAW) generated using gas- and liquid-phase plasma reactors. Plasma was generated using argon, nitrogen, or oxygen as working gases and titanium or silver electrodes. The treatment time was 7 min at 30 kV. The pH, conductivity, temperature, and concentrations of H2O2, NO3−, and NO2− were determined immediately after treatment and after 7 days of storage at 4 °C. Antimicrobial activity was evaluated against Listeria monocytogenes, Salmonella enterica, and Candida utilis after 3 and 24 h of contact. Plasma treatment increased the concentrations of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species. Antimicrobial efficacy was microorganism-dependent and was generally highest for PAW generated in the liquid-phase reactor using a silver electrode. Reductions of up to 5.40 log CFU/mL for S. enterica and 6.68 log CFU/mL for C. utilis were achieved. Storage generally reduced antimicrobial efficacy. PAW demonstrated significant antimicrobial potential, with reactor configuration and electrode material being important determinants of its efficacy. Complementary biological assays indicated no detectable cytotoxicity in the MTT assay, while selected PAW samples exhibited membrane-related and pro-oxidative effects.</jats:p>
title: Influence of Plasma Reactor Configuration on the Physicochemical Properties, Stability, and Biological Activity of Plasma-Activated Water

<jats:p>Objetivo: Determinar la correlación entre el Índice Aterogénico del Plasma (IAP) y el Péptido Natriurético tipo B (BNP) en pacientes con Insuficiencia Cardíaca Crónica Agudizada.


Material y métodos: Estudio transversal, correlacional, analítico. A través de un muestreo no probabilístico, fueron evaluados pacientes con insuficiencia cardíaca crónica agudizada, con medición al ingreso de BNP, perfil de lípidos y a quienes fue realizado un ecocardiograma transtorácico durante su hospitalización.


Resultados: Fueron estudiados 30 pacientes con insuficiencia cardíaca agudizada. La mediana de los niveles de BNP al ingreso fue de 764.5 pg/mL, la mediana del IAP fue de 0.51. La media de la fracción de eyección del ventrículo izquierdo (FEVI) obtenida fue de 38%, todos los pacientes presentaron algún grado de disfunción diastólica: el 50% grado 1, el 33.3% grado 2 y sólo el 16.6% grado 3. El coeficiente de correlación de Spearman para el BNP e IAP fue de -0,02213, con un valor de p=0.5.


Conclusiones: El IAP juega un papel como un factor de riesgo cardiovascular, pero no como parte de la evaluación de los pacientes con Insuficiencia Cardíaca Crónica Agudizada. No existe correlación entre el IAP y BNP.</jats:p>
title: Correlación entre el índice aterogénico del plasma y el péptido natriurético tipo B en pacientes con insuficiencia cardíaca cronica agudizada

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Patients with intracranial meningiomas exhibit an increased risk of venous thromboembolic events (VTE), particularly pulmonary embolisms (PE), with reported incidences of 6-8% and mortality of 10-14%. Postoperative PE represents a potentially life-threatening complication and may delay recovery or adjuvant treatment. Early detection of both symptomatic and subclinical PE is therefore clinically relevant, especially as direct oral anticoagulants have not been shown to increase postoperative hemorrhage risk in this setting. This study evaluated postoperative D-dimer levels as a pragmatic tool for PE risk stratification following meningioma surgery.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>All patients undergoing meningioma resection between 2019 and 2025 with D-dimer measurement on postoperative day 3 were retrospectively analyzed. Cut-off values were adopted from Inoue et al. Patients with D-dimer levels &gt;8.2 mg/L underwent CT angiography and lower extremity venous ultrasound. Values between 5.5-8.2 mg/L were reassessed on the following day; further diagnostics were performed only in cases of rising levels. PE-positive and PE-negative groups were compared using the Mann-Whitney U and Welch t-tests. Sensitivity and specificity were calculated for different cut-offs.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Twenty-nine patients were included. PE was detected in 20.7%, with 66% presenting with dyspnea or tachycardia. No deep vein thrombosis was identified. Median D-dimer levels were significantly higher in PE-positive patients (15.79 mg/L, CI 11.47-19.22) compared to PE-negative patients (2.43 mg/L, CI 1.58-3.4) (p &lt; 0.01). WHO grading showed no association (p = 1). A cut-off of 5 mg/L achieved 100% sensitivity and 83% specificity, while 8 mg/L achieved 83% sensitivity and 100% specificity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Postoperative D-dimer assessment after meningioma resection appears suitable for PE detection and allows clinically meaningful risk stratification. Larger studies are required to validate these findings. Structured postoperative D-dimer screening may support implementation of standardized diagnostic algorithms.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: EP13.24 Association of postoperative D-dimer plasma levels with pulmonary embolism after meningioma surgery

items.abstract: <jats:p>Energy disaggregation, also known as non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM), aims to estimate appliance-level power consumption from aggregate measurements collected by a single household meter, enabling fine-grained energy analytics for smart-home and smart-city applications. Existing NILM methods often rely on extensive appliance-level annotations and may suffer performance degradation when transferred across households, due to variations in appliance characteristics, operating modes, and user behavior. To address these challenges, we propose LASER-NILM, a target-local adaptation framework that constructs target-conditioned fine-tuning samples without requiring target appliance-level labels. Specifically, LASER-NILM identifies a source household with appliance activation patterns similar to those of the target household, then synthesizes target-conditioned aggregate–appliance training pairs by inserting matched source activations into the target household’s aggregate measurements. These synthesized samples are used to fine-tune a pre-trained disaggregation model locally with an activation-aware loss function, allowing the model to better capture target household consumption characteristics while avoiding the transmission of target aggregate measurements during adaptation. Experiments on REFIT show that LASER-NILM improves the MAE and SAE performance of WaveNet, BGRU, and Transformer baselines from 1.1% to 16.4% and 4.2% to 65.3%, demonstrating its applicability across different backbone architectures. Cross-dataset evaluation on UK-DALE further shows that LASER-NILM achieves lower overall MAE and SAE than direct transfer and two domain adaptation baselines.</jats:p>
title: LASER-NILM: Local Activation Synthesis for Energy Disaggregation Refinement

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>For more than half a century, influenza antibody immunity has been interpreted through bulk serology, hemagglutinin (HA) titers, and, more recently, cellular B‐cell repertoires. This review argues that protective immunity requires a more integrated view of cellular, plasma, functional, and predictive antibody repertoires. Single‐cell BCR sequencing, monoclonal antibody cloning, antibody proteomics, and analyses of antibody cooperation now show that memory B cells, plasmablasts, long‐lived plasma cells, circulating IgG, and immune complexes are related but non‐equivalent compartments. Plasma antibody responses display recurring fiducial features, including abundance hierarchies, lineage persistence, donor‐specific dominance, recall‐biased remodeling, and incomplete correspondence with cellular repertoires. These principles are illustrated by HA‐head and HA‐stem antibodies, neuraminidase‐directed immunity, public antibody classes, DR‐motif NA active‐site antibodies, and the concept of public plasma immunity. We emphasize that secreted antibodies are Fc‐liberated molecules capable of engaging complement, C1q, Fc receptors, immune‐complex pathways, and synergistic interactions within polyclonal antibody pools. The next frontier is to define functional and protective repertoires, and to use AI‐guided sequence‐to‐function models to predict antibody breadth, abundance, persistence, Fc activity, cooperation, and protection. Such integration may help transform universal influenza vaccine design from the discovery of exceptional antibodies toward the rational engineering of durable protective repertoires.</jats:p>
title: Influenza Antibody Repertoires: Linking Cellular, Plasma, and Protective Immunity

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates laser-modified glass surface designed to enhance the self-cleaning capabilities of photovoltaic (PV) panels. Soda-lime glass samples were patterned using nanosecond fiber laser processing to create horseshoes like microstructures. Subsequent heat treatment, assisted by silicone oil, was employed to further modify the surface chemistry and optimize wettability. The wetting behavior was systematically analyzed through contact angle measurements, which showed a significant increase from approximately 49° (untreated) to 88.246°, indicating the achievement of wettability transition. Surface profilometry confirmed topographical changes, with increased average roughness after silicone-assisted thermal treatment, suggesting partial filling of surface valleys. SEM confirmed the smoothness due to thermal treatment whereas EDS analysis confirmed the variation in silicon and oxygen composition. Transmittance analysis revealed that laser processing had minimal impact on optical transparency, preserving over 80% transmittance. The combined effect of laser texturing and surface chemistry alteration demonstrates a promising pathway for developing functional glass surfaces with high self-cleaning potential, suitable for solar panel applications in dusty environments.</jats:p>
title: Wettability Control of Laser-Textured Glass via Thermal Treatment

items.abstract: <jats:p>Seminal plasma not only supplies nutrients and energy to spermatozoa but also constitutes the microenvironment for sperm survival. Seminal plasma metabolomics has emerged as a promising approach for reflecting semen quality and exploring the biomarkers of sperm damage. Therefore, elucidating the relationships between seminal plasma metabolites and sperm quality parameters is important. Techniques such as nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS), and liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS) can be used to quantify seminal plasma metabolites in male infertility patients and fertile men. By conducting principal component analysis, correlation analysis, differential metabolite analysis, and pathway enrichment analysis on the obtained data, the differential metabolites in seminal plasma from different patients can be examined. Growing evidence indicates that various differential metabolites in seminal plasma are closely associated with different sperm quality parameters. For instance, metabolites such as carnitine, citrate, and lactate are correlated with sperm motility and concentration. The lipid metabolites phosphatidylcholine and sphingolipids are involved in maintaining sperm membrane integrity, and their abnormalities may affect sperm morphology and function. Currently, most studies have only reported the correlation between differential metabolites and a specific sperm abnormality, and there is a lack of research on the specific molecular mechanisms by which metabolites regulate sperm quality. In the future, investigations on the relationships between seminal plasma metabolites and sperm function‐related parameters should be conducted, and a multiomic approach should be used to identify new biomarkers reflecting sperm quality, thereby providing potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets for male infertility.</jats:p>
title: Seminal Plasma Metabolites and Sperm Quality: A Narrative Review

items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) has historically been considered for antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (AAV) with severe kidney or pulmonary involvement. National inpatient use after publication of the Plasma Exchange in Vasculitis (PEXIVAS) trial remains incompletely characterized.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conducted a repeated cross-sectional analysis of adult National Inpatient Sample hospitalizations from 2016 through 2023. The primary AAV cohort used stable International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. We estimated survey-weighted annual and era-specific TPE use and age- and sex-adjusted era associations. Lupus nephritis (LN) served as a temporal comparator in an adjusted cohort-by-era model. Sensitivity analyses examined principal-diagnosis AAV, AKI, AKI requiring acute kidney replacement therapy (AKI-D), coded pulmonary hemorrhage, and length of stay greater than 1 day.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The cohort included 20,866 AAV hospitalizations and 623 TPE events. Weighted TPE use declined from 4% in 2016–2019 to 2% in 2022–2023; the adjusted later-versus-baseline odds ratio (OR) was 0.49 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.39–0.62). Standardized TPE probabilities declined from 3.81% to 1.91% for AAV and from 1.04% to 0.68% for LN. The absolute difference-in-changes was −1.54 percentage points (95% CI, −2.15 to −0.94), whereas the interaction OR was 0.75 (95% CI, 0.52–1.10; P = 0.14). Baseline-to-later TPE use declined from 14% to 7% in principal-diagnosis AAV, 35% to 14% in AKI-D, and 32% to 23% with coded pulmonary hemorrhage. The length-of-stay-greater-than-1-day result was similar to the primary analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Inpatient TPE use among U.S. AAV hospitalizations declined during 2016–2023, including in multiple coded clinical-context sensitivities. The decline aligned with evolving trial evidence and guidelines, although these data cannot establish causation or appropriateness of treatment decisions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Therapeutic Plasma Exchange Use among ANCA-Associated Vasculitis Hospitalizations after PEXIVAS and Guidelines, 2016–2023

                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>From January 2022 to August 2024, 98 patients with eligible brain metastases were enrolled and treated with robot-assisted LITT. The primary efficacy endpoint was the successful ablation rate, defined as all lesions are ablated of more than 90%. Secondary efficacy endpoints included ablation rate, Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) score at 1, 3, and 6 months post-operation, and overall survival. The safety endpoint was the incidence of postoperative complications.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 130 intracranial lesions were found in the 98 patients, with a mean volume of 3.55 ± 3.48 cm³. 25 patients (25.51%) had multiple lesions, and 48 patients (48.98%) had lesions located in functional areas. Postoperative assessment showed that 92 (93.88%) patients achieved successful ablation. Mean ablation rate was 94.15±10.26%, The KPS scores at 1, 3, and 6 months post-surgery were 90 [80-100], 90 [80-100], and 90 [60-90], respectively; the median overall survival was 15.8 [8.5-23.8] months, and the 1-year survival rate was 63.8%. A total of 4 patients (4.08%) experienced 5 postoperative complications.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>LITT is a safe and effective procedure for treating brain metastases and can provide a new option for the systemic treatment. LITT can achieve a favorable outcome comparable to surgical treatment, and its minimally invasive and safe characteristics make it worthy further application.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: EP07.03 Clinical characteristics and prognosis of magnetic resonance-guided laser interstitial thermal therapy for brain metastases

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Accurate molecular classification of central nervous system (CNS) tumors is essential for diagnosis, treatment stratification, and disease monitoring. Aberrant DNA methylation is a hallmark of CNS tumors and circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation profiling represents a promising non-invasive strategy for tumor detection and classification. Here, we evaluated targeted enzymatic methyl-sequencing (EM-seq) of plasma cfDNA as an approach for CNS tumor classification and discrimination from healthy controls.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A capture panel was designed using public methylation array data and applied for targeted EM-seq. Assay performance was benchmarked against Illumina DNA methylation arrays using matched tumor samples. The study included matched plasma and tumor tissue samples from different CNS subgroups, pediatric patient-derived glioma stem cell lines together with plasma samples from 10 healthy controls.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Comparative analysis of EM-seq and Illumina methylation array data demonstrated a strong correlation (&gt;0.96) and showed concordant copy-number alteration profiles across platforms. Principal component analysis-derived marker scores showed clear subgroup-related structure. These findings support the biological relevance of the plasma DNA methylation signal and its ability to capture tumor subgroup-specific information. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed robust classification performance. In multiclass one-vs-rest analyses, discrimination was strongest for lymphoma and meningioma, reaching AUC of 0.94, whereas distinction for IDH-mutant and IDH-wildtype gliomas was more modest (0.7 and 0.8, respectively). Pairwise analyses showed high accuracy across subgroups, with AUCs reaching 1.0 for IDH-mutant glioma versus lymphoma and IDH-wildtype glioma versus meningioma. Plasma cfDNA also distinguished CNS tumors from healthy controls with high accuracy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our study demonstrates that plasma cfDNA methylation signatures can provide a potential framework for liquid biopsy-based CNS tumor classification, distinguish patients with CNS tumors from healthy individuals and provide a promising basis for longitudinal monitoring and post-surgical follow-up.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Funding</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This work was supported by the Swedish Childhood Cancer Foundation, the Swedish Research Council, the Swedish Cancer Society, Assar Gabrielsson Foundation, SU Fund, Lions Cancerfond väst, Wilhelm & Martina Lundgren Foundation, and Lindhés Advokatbyrå Foundation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: P05.05.A Targeted EM-seq of plasma cfDNA reveals methylation signatures for CNS tumor classification and Monitoring

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Nanosecond pulsed laser coloring of AISI 304 stainless steel is investigated to reproduce continuous-tone color images. In conventional laser coloring, simple color patterns are mainly generated within a restricted color range, and precise control of hue and tone remains difficult. To address this limitation, a laser-based surface functionalization method is proposed for pixel-by-pixel reproduction of complex color images. A multilevel micronano structure is developed to construct colors in an assembled state, allowing for more accurate and detailed color rendering. The modulation of hue and tone of mixed colors is systematically investigated with respect to primary color combinations and their proportions within image pixels, uncovering their impact on color representation. An adaptive approach for distributing primary color proportions is introduced, based on spectral features and color components, to enable diversified color generation and precise control over both hue and tone. Experimental results show that the proposed method improves color restoration, hue richness, and tonal subtlety compared with existing laser coloring methods, providing an ink-free route to durable, microstructure-controlled colored surfaces for applications in display imaging, surface decoration, and color printing.</jats:p>

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Erectile dysfunction (ED) secondary to ischiocavernosus muscle (ICM) injury is a significant yet frequently underestimated complication in survivors of pelvic fractures. Given the suboptimal outcomes of conventional therapies, this study sought to investigate the adjunctive therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) combined with suturing across different intervention time points in a rat model of bilateral ischiocavernosus muscle excision (BICME).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 48 male SPF Sprague-Dawley rats were subjected to BICME and assigned to three intervention time-points: immediate (G0), 4 weeks (G4w), and 8 weeks (G8w) post-injury. Each time-point contained four subgroups: Sham, BICME, BICME + Suturing, and BICME + Suturing + PRP. Erectile function was quantitatively assessed via the ratio of intracavernous pressure to mean arterial pressure (ICP/MAP). Histological examinations including hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, Masson's trichrome staining, immunofluorescence (MYH4, fibronectin), and Western blot (MyoD, synaptophysin) were performed to assess myofiber regeneration, fibrotic scar formation, and presynaptic-related protein expression. Two-way ANOVA was applied for statistical analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      BICME induced severe ED accompanied by impaired muscle regeneration and excessive fibrosis. At matched time-points, BICME + Suturing + PRP significantly elevated ICP/MAP values, increased myofiber number and diameter, up-regulated MYH4 and MyoD expression, and reduced collagen-fibronectin-positive fibrotic area compared with the BICME + Suturing group (
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       &lt; 0.05). Synaptophysin expression was also markedly increased after PRP combined treatment. Suturing yielded the best therapeutic outcomes at G4w, whereas suturing plus PRP achieved maximal benefits when administered at G0.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>PRP-assisted suturing repair of ICM injury improves erectile function in BICME rats, likely by promoting myofiber regeneration, attenuating fibrosis, and possibly facilitating presynaptic/neuromuscular junction remodeling. Immediate post-injury application of PRP with suturing achieved the best therapeutic effect. These findings suggest that PRP is a promising regenerative strategy for ED associated with ICM injury after pelvic fracture.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Platelet-rich plasma-assisted repair of ischiocavernosus muscle injury improves erectile dysfunction in a rat model

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Urine has emerged as a promising non-invasive source of circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) in neuro-oncology, but the extent to which its molecular features reflect those observed in plasma remains unclear. Identifying which cfDNA features are conserved across samples versus sample-specific is essential for accurate interpretation of urine-derived signals and for the design of liquid biopsy approaches in brain tumors.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Genome-wide cfDNA profiling was performed using Oxford Nanopore sequencing on matched plasma and urine samples from 20 patients with high-grade gliomas. The paired within-patient design enabled direct intra-individual comparison between body fluids. We analyzed a broad panel of fragmentomic and epigenomic features, including fragment length patterns, sequence composition, copy number variation profiles, mutation calls, and methylation marks (5mC, 5hmC), to identify conserved and sample-specific signals.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Initial comparison of matched plasma and urine samples revealed differences in fragment length distributions between the two sample types, suggesting distinct fragmentation or degradation processes in each compartment, while preserving tumor-derived signals across compartments. Coverage analysis of glioma-relevant genes showed variable patterns, with some genes covered preferentially in plasma and others in urine, indicating sample-specific representation of tumor-associated regions. Mapping quality was comparable between matched plasma and urine samples. Analysis of additional fragmentomic and epigenomic features is ongoing.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These preliminary findings suggest that plasma and urine capture partially overlapping but non-identical cfDNA signals in glioma patients. Further analysis across the full feature panel will clarify which characteristics are conserved between plasma and urine, and provide a basis for informed feature selection in future computational and machine learning approaches in neuro-oncology.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Support</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Project titled “Liquid Biopsy and Machine Learning for Early Detection of High-Grade Gliomas” is carried out within the First Team programme of the Foundation for Polish Science, co-financed by the European Union under the European Funds for Smart Economy 2021-2027 (FENG).*JZ and UL contributed equally</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: P04.01.A Conserved and Sample-Specific cfDNA Features in Matched Plasma and Urine from Glioma Patients

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Purpura fulminans (PF) is a rare, life-threatening emergency defined by rapidly progressive cutaneous necrosis driven by microvascular thrombosis and severe disruption of natural anticoagulant pathways. Published series report in-hospital mortality of 40%–44% and amputation rates approaching 80% in survivors. The relationship between the timing of fresh frozen plasma (FFP) initiation and outcome has not been described, and inflammatory leukocyte indices have not been evaluated in this disease.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This was a retrospective single-center case series of adult patients who were diagnosed with PF between 2009 and 2026. Demographics, body surface area (BSA) affected, symptom duration before FFP initiation, comprehensive inflammatory and coagulation laboratory markers, comorbidities, and clinical outcomes [in-hospital mortality, surgical intervention, intensive care unit (ICU) admission, ICU duration] were recorded. Given the sample size, all analyses were exploratory and descriptive.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A total of 9 cases were identified. The median age was 49 years (IQR 39–57; 6F/3M). In-hospital mortality was 44.4% (4/9), surgical intervention was required in 55.6% (5/9), and 33.3% (3/9) were admitted to the ICU. Endocrinopathy was present in 77.8% of patients [hypothyroidism
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 4, hyperthyroidism
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 2, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 1]; all four deaths occurred in patients with endocrinopathy, while both patients without endocrinopathy survived without surgery. All three patients who received FFP within 3 days of symptom onset survived without surgical intervention (0% mortality, 0% surgery), compared with 67% mortality and 83% surgery in the six patients with delayed FFP (&gt;3 days; Fisher's exact
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = 0.048 for surgical intervention; mortality
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = 0.167). Lower platelet count was associated with surgical intervention (Mann–Whitney
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = 0.016; Spearman
                      <jats:italic>ρ</jats:italic>
                      =−0.866,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = 0.003). Longer symptom duration before FFP showed near-complete descriptive separation between patients with and without surgery (AUC=0.975). Higher MLR showed descriptive separation for mortality (AUC=0.850) and ICU admission (AUC=0.833). D-dimer correlated most strongly with BSA extent (
                      <jats:italic>ρ</jats:italic>
                      =0.867,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = 0.002).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this small exploratory series, FFP initiation within ≤3 days of symptom onset coincided with the absence of death and surgical intervention. Because earlier FFP may also reflect earlier presentation, earlier diagnosis or less advanced disease, this observed timing pattern cannot be interpreted causally. Lower platelet count and higher MLR showed exploratory associations with adverse outcomes that require confirmation in larger cohorts. The high prevalence of endocrinopathy warrants prospective investigation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Exploratory associations between inflammatory indices, timing of plasma therapy, and outcomes in adult purpura fulminans: a retrospective case series

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) has emerged as a promising minimally invasive biomarker in solid tumors. In primary brain tumors, however, the blood-brain barrier and tumor-specific biological characteristics may limit the detectability and interpretation of plasma-derived biomarkers. Quantitative cfDNA levels and fragment length patterns in plasma from patients with CNS tumors remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to investigate cfDNA concentrations and fragment length distributions in plasma from patients with benign and malignant brain tumors.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Between April 2022 and March 2024, plasma samples were prospectively collected from patients with intracranial tumors and healthy controls. cfDNA was isolated from preoperative EDTA plasma using the QIAamp Circulating Nucleic Acid Kit (Qiagen). Concentrations were determined using the Qubit dsDNA HS assay (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and were calculated as ng per ml plasma. Fragment length distributions were analyzed using the Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity DNA Assay (Agilent Technologies).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study included 25 controls, 71 patients with meningioma, and 51 patients with glioblastoma. Plasma cfDNA concentrations differed significantly between groups, showing a stepwise increase from controls (11.44 ng/ml) to meningiomas (18.24 ng/ml) and glioblastomas (21.55 ng/ml) (Kruskal-Wallis test, p = 0.0003). cfDNA fragment lengths both in meningioma and glioblastoma patients showed significantly shorter mononucleosomal cfDNA fragments compared with controls (p &lt; 0.05).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Plasma cfDNA concentrations differ significantly between controls and patients with benign and malignant CNS tumors. Furthermore, fragment length analysis with the Agilent Bioanalyzer showed shortening of cfDNA fragments in meningioma and glioblastoma patients. Our findings support the potential of plasma cfDNA as a biomarker in CNS tumors.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: MO04.5.A Plasma cell-free DNA concentrations and fragment length alterations in meningioma and glioblastoma patients

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Current diagnostic approaches for Glioblastoma (GBM), including MRI and surgical biopsy, remain limited in their ability to detect early-stage disease. Liquid biopsy strategies have shown promise but are hindered by an incomplete understanding of early tumourigenesis at the molecular level. Preclinical models that better recapitulate tumour initiation are therefore essential to advance our understanding and facilitate the discovery of highly sensitive and specific biomarkers for early detection. Our previous work using the GL261 model demonstrated that the Nano-omics approach can detect GBM-associated plasma proteomic alterations with &gt;30% concordance with tumour tissue and validation in patient-derived samples, supporting its translational potential.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We applied our previously established Nano-omics integrative workflow to longitudinally profile plasma and tumour tissue proteomes in a genetically engineered murine model of gliomagenesis (RCAS/tv-a system). Glioma formation was induced via PDGFB overexpression and TP53 loss. Matched plasma and brain tissue samples were collected from male and female tumour-bearing mice and stratified into early (0-5 mm³), intermediate (5-20 mm³), and late (≥20 mm³) disease stages based on tumour area in H&E-stained sections, and subsequently analysed using LC-MS/MS-based proteomics.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this study, longitudinal profiling in a tumourigenesis-driven model revealed dynamic, stage-dependent alterations in the plasma proteome during early disease development, including at pre-lesional stages confirmed by PCR detection of integrated proviral DNA. Integration with tumour tissue provided mechanistic insight into the biological processes driving tumour initiation and progression and their reflection in the plasma proteome. Ongoing analysis aims to utilise this mechanism-driven biomarker discovery pipeline to identify highly specific biomarkers of early detection and disease monitoring which will be subject to validation in a human clinical cohort.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This work leverages a disease-relevant model of gliomagenesis to advance mechanism-driven biomarker discovery for early detection. The Nano-omics integrative approach represents a promising strategy for developing liquid biopsy tools that complement imaging protocols and enable the detection of high-grade gliomas before clinical symptoms prevail, allowing more effective intervention and improved patient outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: P18.14.B Longitudinal Nano-omics profiling of the plasma and tumour tissue proteomes to unveil early detection and disease monitoring biomarkers in a gliomagenesis mouse model

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM) engages in a complex interplay with the host immune system to establish a permissive, tumor-supportive milieu. Its tumor microenvironment is considered immunologically “cold,” characterized by profound T-cell suppression. In addition to local immune evasion, GBM patients exhibit systemic immunosuppression, including marked lymphopenia and sequestration of leukocytes within the bone marrow. Collectively, these mechanisms likely contribute to the limited success of current immunotherapeutic strategies in glioma treatment. A deeper understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms may therefore facilitate the development of more effective therapeutic approaches.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A prospective cohort study was conducted including 30 patients with newly diagnosed IDH-wildtype GBM. Platelet-free EDTA blood plasma was collected at baseline and compared with samples from 25 matched healthy controls. Extracellular RNA profiling was performed using total RNA library preparation and massively parallel short read sequencing. Differential gene expression analysis was subsequently carried out.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 531 genes were found to be significantly dysregulated (adjusted p &lt; 0.05), of which 301 were higher and 230 lower expressed in patients compared to controls. Within the innate immune system, key pathways—including Toll-like receptor (TLR), stimulator of interferon genes (STING), and mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein (MAVS)—were lower abundant. This was associated with reduced activation of pro-inflammatory transcriptional programs mediated by NF-κB, STAT1, IRF1, and IRF5. In the adaptive immune compartment, evidence of both T- and B-cell dysfunction was observed, including impaired thymocyte maturation. Gene abundance patterns indicated enrichment of regulatory and exhausted T-cell phenotypes. With respect to the tumor microenvironment, transcriptomic profiling revealed a heterogeneous gene abundance signature associated with the mobilization and differentiation of myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSC), as well as polarization of tumor-associated macrophages (TAM) towards an M2 phenotype.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Patients with GBM exhibit profound systemic and local immunosuppression. Plasma RNA transcriptomic profiling provides a comprehensive view on the molecular pathways underlying this immunosuppressive state. These findings highlight potential targets for the development of novel immunotherapeutic strategies in glioma treatment.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: P12.18.B Plasma RNA transcriptomic profiling reveals molecular pathways related to immunosuppression in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Confocal laser endomicroscopy (CLE) enables real-time intraoperative tissue assessment in neuro-oncology. However, its clinical performance might depend on image acquisition quality and operator experience, often resulting in a substantial proportion of non-interpretable images. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate temporal trends in image quality, acquisition efficiency, and concordance with histopathology.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients undergoing surgery for high-grade intra-axial tumors, including glioblastoma and brain metastases, between June 2023 and January 2026. A subgroup of patients with paired CLE imaging and histopathology was included . Temporal trends were assessed by year, focusing on image quality (motion- and blood-related artifacts), proportion of non-interpretable images, proportion of useful images, number of images per case, and concordance with histopathology.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 29 cases were included. Image acquisition quality improved over time, with a decrease in motion-related artifacts despite an initial increase (10.5% in 2023, 15.8% in 2024, and 4.3% in 2025), while blood-related artifacts showed a slight increase and subsequent stabilization (6.0% in 2023, 8.3% in 2024, and 8.3% in 2025). The proportion of useful images increased overall (48% [n = 39] in 2023, 46% in 2024 [n = 37], and 66% [n = 41] in 2025). The number of images per case initially increased and subsequently decreased (mean 320 in 2023, 520 in 2024, and 270 in 2025), suggesting improved acquisition efficiency. Concordance between CLE and histopathology also improved over time, with a reduction in discordant cases (n = 4 in 2023, n = 2 in 2024, and n = 0 in 2025). These findings reflect progressive optimization of both image acquisition and interpretation in clinical practice. However, histopathological sampling was not blinded to CLE findings, introducing potential selection bias and limiting formal accuracy estimation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>CLE performance improves over time, with measurable gains in image quality, efficiency, and concordance with histopathology, despite a reduction in the number of images acquired per case. These findings support the integration of CLE into routine neuro-oncological surgery, although prospective studies with blinded sampling are required to establish its diagnostic accuracy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: EP03.38 Temporal improvement in image acquisition quality and concordance using intraoperative confocal laser endomicroscopy in brain tumors

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Color center spins in diamond nanostructures are a key resource for emerging quantum technologies. Their innate surface proximity makes precise control of diamond surface chemistry essential for optimizing their functionality and charge states. However, conventional surface functionalization methods provide limited control over the resulting surface termination and color-center charge state. Here, we demonstrate nonvolatile tuning of diamond’s surface termination through laser-induced oxidation of H-terminated diamond nanopillars. By tracking negatively charged silicon-vacancy (SiV
                    <jats:sup>−</jats:sup>
                    ) photoluminescence as a charge-state proxy, we elucidate the carrier-assisted nature of this photocatalytic process through systematic photon-flux and photon-energy analyses, identifying defect charge cycling as a source of photogenerated carriers that drive the interfacial redox chemistry responsible for surface oxidation. Our results suggest that this approach may be applicable to other color centers and host materials for charge-state control and surface engineering in solid-state quantum devices.
                  </jats:p>
title: Photocatalytic control of diamond color center charge states via laser-induced surface oxidation

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Identifying tumour infiltration at resection margins is the primary intraoperative challenge in glioma surgery. Confocal laser endomicroscopy (CLE) enables intraoperative real-time cellular imaging, but its diagnostic value relative to white-light microscopy (WL) and sodium fluorescein (NaF) has not been formally compared in a prospective setting across both primary and recurrent disease.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In a prospective single-centre diagnostic accuracy study, 54 consecutive patients undergoing craniotomy for intracranial neoplasms — including primary tumours and reoperations for recurrent high-grade gliomas (HGG) — were enrolled. Resection margins were assessed sequentially with WL, NaF (YELLOW 560 filter), and CLE (ZEISS CONVIVO®) at the same anatomical site prior to biopsy for frozen section analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A total of 209 specimens were obtained; 133 (63.6%) were tumour-positive on frozen section, which served as the reference standard. The operating surgeon was blinded to pathological results; the neuropathologist was blinded to all imaging findings. CLE achieved the highest sensitivity (83.3%) and accuracy (73.9%), significantly outperforming NaF in accuracy and both WL and NaF in sensitivity and positive predictive value (all p ≤ 0.014). In multivariate mixed-effects analysis, CLE (OR 7.78, p = 0.002) and WL (OR 3.42, p = 0.035) were independent predictors of tumour infiltration; NaF was not significant after mutual adjustment. CLE identified histologically confirmed tumour in 65% of sites where both WL and NaF were simultaneously negative. The combined three-method model achieved AUC 0.933. CLE performance was robust across glioblastoma and lower-grade gliomas, but reduced in brain metastases (AUC 0.583). In the recurrent HGG subgroup, a negative CLE result reduced the post-test probability of tumour infiltration from 65% to 31%, while negative NaF and WL findings provided no discriminative value above baseline prevalence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>CLE proved superior to WL and NaF for the detection of tumour infiltration at the resection margin across primary neoplasms and recurrent gliomas. A negative CLE result provides clinically meaningful guidance in the recurrent setting, where fluorescence offers no incremental benefit. Sequential multimodal assessment combining all three methods maximises diagnostic accuracy and should be integrated into the neuro-oncological surgical workflow.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: OS13.7.A Confocal laser endomicroscopy outperforms white light and sodium fluorescein for tumour margin assessment in glioma surgery: the Florence experience

items.abstract: <jats:p>Emulating long-distance light propagation on a laboratory scale is essential for the ground-based testing of intersatellite optical systems. To address this challenge, we propose and analyze an optical system called the range emulator (RE) to reproduce the spatial propagation effects of a long-distance beam within a compact apparatus. Our analysis identifies the three-lens solutions that implement the RE. Through a numerical exploration, we quantify the fundamental trade-off between system compactness and manufacturing precision. This work provides a practical framework for designing compact optical testbeds for future multi-satellite laser link technologies.</jats:p>
title: Range emulator: a compact paraxial optical system to emulate long-distance monochromatic laser propagation

items.abstract: <jats:p>With the increasing demand for engineering protection and equipment weight reduction, the research and development of lightweight and high-energy-absorbing structures is becoming increasingly urgent. The Menger sponge fractal structure, through its self-similar hierarchical configuration, undergoes multi-stage crushing and is one of the ideal topologies for achieving the coordinated regulation of stiffness and energy absorption. To reveal the influence of fractal order on the compression mechanical behavior and energy absorption characteristics of the Menger sponge fractal structures (MFCs), in this experiment, multi-order MFC specimens of AlSi10Mg were prepared using SLM. After tensile calibration of the same batch of substrate, quasi-static compression, DIC observation and finite element simulation were carried out. The results show that with a fractal dimension of FD = 2.727, the MFC specimens exhibit typical hierarchical crushing and multi-stage plateau characteristics. Strain localization begins at the edge of the aperture and is transmitted layer by layer along the secondary rods. With the increase of order, the initial stiffness decreases from 133.03 kN/mm to 46.97 kN/mm, and the equivalent elastic modulus decreases from 4.93 GPa to 1.74 GPa. The equivalent modulus and the elastic limit decay power-law with relative density. The decay is caused by the coupling of four mechanisms: geometric dilution, bending dominant deformation, stress concentration at the hole edge, and forming defects. The specific energy absorption shows a pattern of first increasing and then decreasing. The specific energy absorption of the second-order MFC is the best (60.32 J/g, which is 65.2% higher than that of the first order). Through experiments and simulations, the optimal order is the second order. The above results provide a reference for the order design and material-process selection of metal fractal energy-absorbing structures for protective engineering.</jats:p>
title: Quasi-static mechanical properties of AlSi10Mg menger sponge fractal structures fabricated by selective laser melting

items.abstract: <jats:p>We study the entanglement among helicity degrees of freedom in QED scattering processes at fixed momentum, modeled as quantum maps whose spectral structure determines the associated entanglement dynamics. We show that, for fermion–fermion scatterings, parity invariance preserves maximal entanglement and generically leads to entanglement saturation under iteration of the maps. The structure of the maps also provides an accurate description of the entanglement dynamics in processes involving both fermions and photons.</jats:p>
title: Characterizing entanglement dynamics in QED scattering processes

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Electrocatalytic alcohol oxidation in direct fuel cells is constrained by CO poisoning and insufficient hydroxyl generation at low potentials. Here we show that anisotropic PtFeCoIrRhCu high‐entropy alloy nanowires with
                    <jats:italic>Lupinus micranthus</jats:italic>
                    ‐like morphology generate a local electric field through coupling of strain‐induced lattice distortion with charge redistribution, enabling a directional capture‐migration‐dissociation relay of interfacial water for efficient low‐potential hydroxyl generation, in which H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O is preferentially captured at Fe/Co sites, migrates under field polarization, and dissociates at Rh/Ir sites. In situ infrared spectroscopy reveals that the electric field reorganizes interfacial water into a more ordered hydrogen‐bond network, facilitating water activation. Density functional theory calculations, differential electrochemical mass spectrometry and operando electrochemical impedance spectroscopy further demonstrate that the generated hydroxyl species accelerate CO oxidative removal and promote the non‐CO oxidation pathway. Consequently, the catalyst achieves a methanol oxidation mass activity of 3.76 A mg
                    <jats:sub>Pt</jats:sub>
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    , 8.36 times that of Pt/C, together with a direct methanol fuel cell peak power density of 163.06 mW cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    and stable membrane‐electrode operation for 200 h at 100 mA cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    . These findings establish strain–charge coupling as a general strategy for engineering interfacial water activation and directing reaction‐pathway selectivity in multimetallic electrocatalysts.
                  </jats:p>
title: Electric‐Field‐Manipulated Reaction Pathway Engineering in Lupinus micranthus ‐Like High‐Entropy Alloy Nanowires for Direct Alcohol Fuel Cells

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to examine the integration of strong and absolute sustainability into urban business education, challenging mainstream economic assumptions that ignore biophysical realities. It explores pedagogical strategies to equip future professionals in the built environment to navigate the tensions between business objectives and planetary limits.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using a practitioner-led action research approach, the instructor redesigned a master’s-level course at Malmö University. Outcomes were evaluated through a mixed-methods analysis, triangulating student questionnaires, instructor teaching journals and thematic analysis of student project outputs and learning reflections.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The curriculum successfully introduced frameworks like the flourishing business model canvas and absolute decarbonisation. However, students found the sobering reality of exceeded planetary boundaries emotionally draining. A primary challenge identified was a chicken-and-egg problem: the lack of existing practical examples for absolute sustainability in business made theoretical conceptualisation difficult. Students also struggled to reconcile long-term ecological timeframes with short-term market pressures and competitive realities.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This research fills a critical gap in business education where strong sustainability remains marginal, particularly within the built environment sector. It provides rare, empirically grounded guidance for educators seeking to move beyond efficiency-based weak sustainability toward transformative learning that prepares students to reshape business logic within the limits of the Anthropocene.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Educating for transformation: embedding strong and absolute sustainability in urban business education

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In cases where a robot must operate autonomously in outdoor environments, such as in agricultural fields, it needs to know its pose (position and orientation) in a global coordinate system. Orientation estimation is usually performed using a magnetometer. However, this type of sensor is susceptible to disturbances from magnetic fields generated by the robot's components and the environment, which can lead to errors in orientation estimation. In this work, a methodology is proposed to estimate the orientation of an agricultural robot using measurements from a magnetic, angular rate, and gravity (MARG) sensor, which consists of an accelerometer, gyroscope, and magnetometer. The procedure involves applying the
                    <jats:italic>Least Squares Ellipsoid Specific Fitting</jats:italic>
                    method to calibrate the magnetometer and correct hard‐ and soft‐iron distortions. Then the Madgwick filter is applied to estimate the robot's orientation from MARG sensor measurements. First, experiments are conducted in a simulation environment, where the behavior of the real robot and sensor measurements are simulated in an artificial soybean field. Compared with real‐world environments, simulation allows for more controlled experiments, enabling variations in sensor noise, sampling frequency, and other conditions. This approach facilitates a precise analysis of the filter and provides an estimate of its minimum error. The results in the simulation environment showed an average error of  and maximum of  for the pitch and roll angles, while the average and maximum error in the yaw estimation was  and , respectively. For the experiments in real‐world environments, data sequences were obtained from an agricultural robot. The results showed an average difference of  to  when compared with a state‐of‐the‐art SLAM system.
                  </jats:p>
title: Absolute Orientation Estimation for Agricultural Robots Through Ellipsoid‐Based Magnetometer Calibration and Madgwick Filter

items.abstract: <jats:p>Strong seismic action frequently triggers catastrophic failure of high and steep slopes, with dynamic response and failure modes governed by geotechnical conditions. Based on the high and steep slope at Section SL17 of the Kathmandu–Terai Expressway in a strong seismic region of Nepal, this study integrates shaking table model tests and three-dimensional finite element simulations to analyze the dynamic response, deformation, and failure processes of the slope, and the reinforcement effectiveness of prestressed anchor cables. The acceleration response exhibits pronounced elevation amplification that increases nonlinearly with height and reaches its maximum near the crest. Under the sequential loading program adopted here, no visible cracks formed up to 0.4 g; the first tensile cracks appeared at 0.5 g, after the specimen had been subjected to the lower levels. This onset therefore reflects cumulative damage and should not be regarded as an intrinsic PGA-only threshold. Once cracking initiated, it developed in the interbedded highly weathered siltstone and mudstone, forming a continuous deep-seated slip surface and leading to global instability. Prestressed anchor cables effectively restrain deformation in the upper part of the slope; in the numerical analysis, they reduce the crest displacement by approximately 29–35% while the PGA amplification factor increases by approximately 9%. In the 0.3 g parametric analysis for the SL17 slope, expanding the anchor cable layout range produced a larger improvement in the safety factor than increasing the prestress or reducing the cable spacing: increasing the number of rows from 5 to 14 raised the safety factor from 1.24 to 1.35, above the value of 1.15 required for this class of slope. At 0.4 g, even the most favorable single-factor schemes fell below 1.15, so these design recommendations are conditional on the 0.3 g case.</jats:p>
title: Dynamic Response and Disaster Prevention of an Anchored High and Steep Slope Under Strong Earthquake Excitation

                    The maximum accelerating field achievable in both normal and superconducting cavities is limited by field emission and vacuum arcs. However, this limit can be extended with a conditioning process and significantly enhanced by operating at cryogenic temperatures. To better understand how vacuum arcs begin and how conditioning improves performance, consistent data across different materials and temperatures are needed. To support this effort, high-voltage tests were carried out on Nb and Ti-6Al-4V electrodes at low temperatures, demonstrating strong ability to withstand high electric fields. Nb electrodes reached fields of

                        <l:mo>/</l:mo>
                        <l:mi mathvariant="normal">m</l:mi>
                      </l:mrow>
                    </l:math>
                    . Regular field emission monitoring is proposed as a diagnostic tool for optimizing conditioning, with variations in the enhancement factor signaling approach to the material’s field limit.

items.abstract: We introduce a novel technique for proving global strong discrete maximum principles for finite element discretizations of linear and semilinear elliptic equations for cases when the common, matrix-based sufficient conditions are not satisfied. The basic argument consists of extending the strong form of discrete maximum principle from macroelements to the entire domain via a connectivity argument. The method is applied to discretizations of elliptic equations with certain pathological meshes, and to semilinear elliptic equations.

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>To address the limitations of low identification accuracy and limited robustness associated with single‐sensor lateral slip detection in hilly and mountainous terrains, an Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF)‐based lateral slip fusion identification framework was proposed. A preliminary lateral slip parameter estimation method based on Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) dynamic resolution was designed, and the spatial geometric relationship between lateral slip and pose transformation was derived. A lateral slip identification algorithm named HYVIO was proposed, which combines a sparse feature optical flow matching mechanism with a ground plane constraint to construct a pose accumulation algorithm for accurate reconstruction of relative lateral slip parameters in agricultural machinery. A multi‐source data fusion architecture based on UKF was constructed, establishing a data fusion equation with an adaptive weight allocation mechanism to achieve optimal estimation of outputs from both the GNSS and HYVIO systems. The precision of lateral slip identification was validated using a constructed slope experiment platform. Fusion experiments demonstrated that the average reduction in RMSE reached 37.5%, which significantly enhances the identification stability and environmental adaptability of the lateral slip identification algorithm in hilly and mountainous environments.</jats:p>
title: A Multi‐Sensor Fusion Framework for Lateral Slip Identification of Agricultural Machinery: Development and Experiment

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Various algorithms have been employed to evaluate the numbers of HLA mismatches to stratify the risk of rejection, but these algorithms often neglect the strength of mismatched peptides in stimulating an immune response. We previously designed the Categorical Amino acid Mismatched Epitope (CAME) algorithm to identify strong binding peptides of mismatched donor HLA‐DQB1.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We applied this algorithm to a large cohort of heart recipients transplanted in our hospital and evaluated the impact of CAME mismatched HLA‐DQB1 on the development of de novo donor specific antibodies and antibody mediated rejection.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We demonstrated that the presence of strong binding peptides was associated with the development of HLA‐DQB1 de novo donor specific antibodies. De novo HLA‐DQB1 donor specific antibodies increased the risk of severe antibody mediated rejection significantly only in recipients with mismatched strong binding peptides identified by the algorithm.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These results suggest that HLA‐DQ mismatches, evaluated by the Categorical Amino acid Mismatched Epitope algorithm, can stratify the risk of de novo donor specific antibody development and rejection in heart transplant recipients.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Strong Immunogenic Mismatched HLA‐DQ in Combination With DQ De Novo Donor Specific Antibodies Predicts Severe Antibody Mediated Rejection
