items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hydrothermal systems have long been proposed as plausible cradles for the chemical origin of life, yet how hydrothermal minerals shape the synthetic potential of prebiotic chemical networks remains poorly understood. Here, we construct a six-layered computational mineral-promoted chemical reaction network (M-CRN) by integrating experimentally validated reactions promoted by minerals into a classical chemical reaction network. We combine machine-learning-assisted pathway analysis with thermodynamic assessment to quantify how these minerals alter the accessibility, connectivity, and energetic properties of prebiotic chemistry. The M-CRN contains 114,476 molecules, including 26 intermediates associated with five proposed primordial metabolic cycles and 10 amino acids selected as target molecules. Compared with a network without minerals, the M-CRN provides more than twice as many enumerated pathways for 12 target molecules, enables access to 14 otherwise inaccessible target molecules, and shortens the synthetic routes to four targets. Metal sulfides also broaden the carbon sources available for assimilatory fixation and chain elongation; under modeled Miller-type conditions, mineral-promoted reactions are more frequent in the network than corresponding non-mineral pathways. These network-level effect suggest that metal sulfides could enhance organic synthesis under resource-limited conditions, with potential implications for the dilution challenge in hydrothermal environments. Mineral-promoted reactions preferentially contribute to the formation of sulfur-containing organic molecules with higher free energies and more diverse subsequent transformations, linking network expansion to potentially energy-rich chemistry. These findings identify hydrothermal metal sulfides as key organizers of prebiotic reaction networks and provide a framework connecting mineral-mediated geochemistry to the emergence of metabolic precursors.</jats:p>
title: Hydrothermal minerals expand the accessible prebiotic chemical space: Insights from computational reaction networks

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This work presents a physics-informed synthetic waveform
  generation and HDL replay validation framework for radiation
  detector readout development. The proposed workflow connects Monte
  Carlo energy deposition modelling, detector-informed waveform
  synthesis, ADC digitization, readout metric analysis and HDL-ready
  replay vector generation within a single reproducible chain.  The
  framework is demonstrated using a NaI(Tl)-based scintillation
  detector reference case for 59.5 keV gamma rays.  Geant4-generated
  deposited energy records are used as the physical input for
  producing truth-labelled NaI(Tl)-like waveform windows, which are
  subsequently digitized at ADC resolutions of 8, 10 and 12 bits. This
  structure allows quantization effects to be separated from detector
  response and noise effects while preserving event-level reference
  information.  For the simulated waveform dataset, energy
  reconstruction is dominated by analog noise and gain variation
  rather than ADC bit-depth, with non-zero-event energy RMSE values
  ranging from approximately 0.86 keV to 1.03 keV over the tested
  noise conditions. The generated ADC vectors are exported for HDL
  replay validation using Icarus Verilog, where the trigger decision,
  peak count and peak index outputs agree with software reference
  labels with zero mismatches across the tested ADC configurations.
  These results establish functional consistency for the tested
  synthetic inputs. The waveform model has not been validated against
  measured NaI(Tl) calibration data, and its synthetic-to-real
  transferability remains unassessed.  A supplementary Vivado
  implementation comparison on an Artix-7 target identifies a severe
  timing violation in the original RTL and demonstrates internal
  timing closure at 250 MHz after explicit arithmetic pipelining.
  The revised 12-bit block achieves worst setup and hold slacks of
  +0.223 and +0.086 ns, respectively, with eight added clock
  cycles of latency; external interface timing and physical board
  operation remain unvalidated.</jats:p>
title: Physics-informed synthetic waveform generation and HDL replay validation for radiation detector readout development

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To report the first evidence of efficacy of interleukin-6 (IL-6) blockade with tocilizumab in radiation-induced brachial plexopathy (RIBP), a rare and disabling late complication of radiotherapy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A single patient with a history of deltoid sarcoma treated with surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy was evaluated decades later for progressive upper limb weakness and paresthesias. Clinical examination, nerve conduction studies/electromyography (NCS/EMG), and brachial plexus MRI were consistent with diagnosis of RIBP. After failure of bevacizumab, the patient received compassionate tocilizumab.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Tocilizumab (162 mg every four weeks for three cycles) was well tolerated and led to partial clinical improvement, including increased muscle strength (≥1 point on MRC scale) and reduced paresthesias. MRI showed decreased contrast enhancement, and NCS/EMG demonstrated functional improvement. Benefits persisted at 18 months.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This case highlights a potential disease-modifying role of IL-6 blockade in RIBP, including in late-stage or treatment-refractory cases. It supports further investigation of tocilizumab as a therapeutic option and suggests IL-6 as a relevant target in radiation-induced plexopathy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: EP08.03 Tocilizumab in Radiation-Induced Plexopathy

<jats:p>A degree-zero charge on ten residue classes can be recovered from its
prime-power ramp at the first seventeen positive integers. A marked
degree-five correspondence on split Tate curves has a transpose of rank one on this
nine-dimensional space. We exhibit a
quadratic character in the kernel and recover its prime-power coefficients
by counting distinct invariant lines of the Fibonacci inflation over finite
fields. With the cyclic-family normalization of the Alpöge--Claude release,
the combined centered sum is the integrated weighted distinct-prime deficit
minus a higher-power correction asymptotic to $(16/7)\sqrt X$. Using the
external integral window theorem, we show that sampled fourth-moment bounds
with arbitrarily small positive exponent loss are equivalent to the
critical-line assertion for $\zeta$ and $L(\cdot,\chi_5)$. An independent arithmetic bound on the
moment remains open.</jats:p>
title: Prime-power ramps on adelic windows and the degree-five Tate correspondence

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Natural rubber (NR) stands as a critical high-strength sustainable elastomer with nearly two centuries of widespread industrial applications. However, conventional processing typically generates random entangled and associative networks, restricting the simultaneous enhancement of strength and toughness. Herein, a strategy is developed to independently regulate entanglement and association densities during latex coalescence by controlling plant protein aggregates. Specifically, compact aggregates induce a tortuosity effect that restrains molecular diffusion for denser entanglements, while loose ones physically bind to the natural terminal groups to construct a high association density. The densified entanglements delocalize stress between cross-links, while the abundant terminal associations enhance the crystallinity and orientation during strain-induced crystallization. Following mild prevulcanization (333 K), this decoupled network design eliminates high-temperature post-curing (&gt;383 K) while affording vulcanizates with enhanced crack growth resistance and &gt;30 MPa tensile strength. This work presents a strategy to overcome the strength–toughness trade-off, offering an energy-efficient pathway for manufacturing sustainable NR latex products, such as dip-molded flexible robotic skins that demonstrate superior crack propagation resistance under dynamic environments.</jats:p>
title: Protein-Mediated Decoupling of Entanglement and Association Densities for Strong and Tough Natural Rubber

items.abstract: <jats:p>Since the possibility of direct, label-free detection of biomolecules using field-effect transistors (FETs) was first proposed around 2000, hundreds to tens of thousands of studies on nanowire/nanoribbon FET (nanoFET) biosensors have followed; yet, aside from the ion-sensitive FET (ISFET) used for pH sensing and FET-based ion sensors employing ion-selective membranes, no FET biosensor has reached actual clinical or commercial use over the past two decades. Building on prior equivalent-circuit and “fake response” analyses of nanoFET read-out, this study re-examines the electrical measurement configuration of nanoFET biosensors and shows that a substantial portion of previously reported “direct detection” signals can be explained not by the target’s own electric field but by gate-leakage current inherent to water-gate architectures and by electrical-double-layer (EDL) potential changes that accompany routine solution exchange. Without a defect-free gate dielectric, the source-drain current necessarily contains a gate-leakage component indistinguishable from the channel-resistance signal; even with an intact gate oxide, the signal is governed not by the charge of the adsorbed target molecules themselves but by the EDL interfacial potential, which is altered by the electrolyte’s ionic strength, pH, and surface chemistry. In nanoFET biosensor research, given that a buffer exchange cannot be avoided in the experimental procedure, the EDL potential change attributable to the target molecule’s own contribution cannot be quantified or converted into target-concentration information—and this difficulty is especially acute near LOD-level concentrations, where it dilutes the very advantage the sensing principle is meant to offer. It is important to understand both the difficulty of distinguishing this from a fake signal arising from gate leakage and why the FET channel-conductance shift itself is difficult to convert into a measure of the target concentration’s contribution alone, given the procedural steps the detection process requires. This is because the target-detection experimental procedure for FET biosensors inherently cannot avoid solution exchange, so the change in EDL potential distribution attributable to target-molecule adsorption cannot be isolated.</jats:p>
title: Operational Flaws in Field-Effect Transistor (FET)-Based Biosensors: Gate-Leakage Current in Water-Gate FET Devices and Fake Field-Effect Signals from Biomolecular Charge

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Microbial enzymes and whole cells convert food-derived precursors into food ingredients under mild conditions, but laboratory conversion alone does not establish food-grade manufacturability. Previous reviews have emphasized catalysts, engineering strategies, or individual products. This critical narrative review complements those perspectives through a descriptive comparison of six transformation classes—hydrolysis and selective deconjugation, glycosylation, epimerization, decarboxylation, redox conversion, and acyl transfer—and their dominant constraints: selectivity, donor supply and economy, equilibrium, pH and salt burden, cofactor balance and product toxicity, or phase behavior and water activity. Detailed analysis then covers five food-ingredient categories—D-allulose, isoquercitrin, γ-aminobutyric acid, vanillin, and structured lipids—represented by six selected product–process–application units. These are assessed using common descriptive categories covering reaction, process, operational, recovery and specification, food-system, and safety, regulatory, and economic evidence. Conversion or titer alone cannot establish manufacturing readiness without realistic loading, catalyst lifetime, isolated-product recovery, product specification, and application evidence. Operational evidence varied across the selected processes, ranging from laboratory-scale catalyst stability measurements to reported pilot- and industrial-scale validation of continuous structured-lipid production. However, complete downstream recovery, finished-ingredient specifications, and process-level economic evidence remained insufficiently documented. Evidence from prolonged operation does not in itself establish isolated-product recovery or performance in the intended food application. No single engineering approach addresses the different constraints of all transformation classes.</jats:p>
title: From Biotransformation to Bioprocess: Bridging Reaction Performance and Manufacturing Feasibility in Microbial Biocatalysis for Food Ingredients

items.abstract: <jats:p>Developed an efficient alternative protocol for the synthesis of 3,4-dihydropyrimidone (DHPMs) derivatives from substituted aldehydes, methyl/ethyl acetoacetate & urea/thiourea in the presence of a protic ionic liquid (PIL) - 1-Methylimidazolium trifluoromethanesulfonate [MIM][OTf]. [MIM][OTf] which acts both as a solvent as well as an efficient catalyst. This protocol offered good yield (81-96%) in very short reaction time (25-75 min.) under optimized mild reaction conditions. Reported catalyst was showed decent profitability up to five cycles. High yield, short reaction time, role of ILs as green solvent and catalyst, recyclable nature of catalyst are some key outcomes of this research work.</jats:p>

                    Numerous articles in recent years indicate an interest in solar tracing technology, emphasizing the tracking mechanisms, sensor integration, and automation techniques to enhance solar energy efficiency. These articles demonstrate that solar tracking systems significantly increases the average yearly energy generation over fixed PV systems. However, these works do not consider anisotropic diffuse radiation to assess the incident solar radiation on PV solar tracking systems. Therefore, the purpose of the present study is to compare the incident diffuse energy of single‐axis tracking systems between isotropic and anisotropic diffuse radiation models to improve the assessed incident solar radiation on the PV systems. In addition, a new obscuring factor is introduced into the anisotropic model. The comparison is performed on north‐south horizontal axis: east‐west tracking and east‐west horizontal axis: north‐south tracking, both using astronomical tracking algorithm. The anisotropic diffuse radiation model predicts 7.68% higher annual diffuse energy and 2.02% higher annual global energy for east‐west tracking, and 12.32% higher annual diffuse energy and 2.81% higher annual global energy for north‐south tracking, than the isotropic model. items.abstract: <jats:p>Geopolymers blended with silica fume (SF) offer enhanced performance, but the influence of the curing sequence on their properties remains unexplored. This study examines, for the first time, the impact of ambient curing (AC) prior to heat curing (HC) on the strength and reaction products of geopolymer mortars (GPMs) based on SF and fly ash (FA), highlighting their process–structure–property relationships. The initial AC periods were 0–48 h, while HC was conducted at 60°C for 48 h and 100°C for 24 h. Under optimal curing conditions, GPM30 with 5% SF achieved a compressive strength of 54 MPa after initial AC for 48 h and HC at 100°C for 24 h. This was an increase of 42% over GPM26 (5% SF), which reached only 37 MPa after direct HC for 24 h, highlighting the benefit of initial AC. X-ray diffraction and Rietveld analysis confirmed the presence of additional crystalline phases of albite, aragonite and anorthite minerals, indicating the formation of a stable, dense geopolymer matrix under optimal curing conditions. The retention of moisture, as indicated by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and attributed to the presence of SF, increased the curing efficiency. The results of this work highlight the correlation between curing, aluminosilicate structure and compressive strength, offering insights into optimising curing conditions for SF-blended FA-based geopolymers.</jats:p>
title: Influence of initial ambient curing on reaction products and strength development in fly ash–silica fume geopolymers

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Electrolysis of water is considered one of the most promising methods for sustainable hydrogen production. However, improving the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) requires the development of efficient non-noble metal electrocatalysts capable of reducing kinetic barriers such as overpotential and accelerating reaction kinetics. Among the various candidates, Ni–P coatings have attracted significant attention due to their excellent electrocatalytic activity toward HER. Here, a hybrid electrocatalytic system based on a NiP electrocatalyst was developed to further enhance HER performance. The proposed catalyst design integrates four key components─activated carbon, polyaniline (PANI), ZnO, and CeO2─to improve the catalytic kinetics and overall electrochemical performance. The fabricated AC/PANI-ZnO-CeO2-NiP electrode exhibited outstanding HER activity in an alkaline medium, demonstrating high stability, a low overpotential of 74 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm–2, and a reduced Tafel slope of 78 mV dec–1. The enhanced performance of the hybrid catalyst is attributed to its increased number of exposed active sites and improved electrical conductivity, which collectively contribute to superior electrocatalytic activity compared to many recently reported analogous systems.</jats:p>
title:
Engineering a Hybrid
AC/PANI–Metal Oxide–NiP
Electrocatalyst Architecture for High-Efficiency Hydrogen Evolution
Reaction

items.abstract: <jats:p>Since 1964, the Groningen gas field in the Netherlands has experienced significant subsidence due to gas extraction. Although satellite radar interferometry (InSAR) has been widely used to estimate the vertical displacements of the field, capturing the full three-dimensional deformation, including omnidirectional horizontal components, remained a challenge and has only been achieved from spatially sparse observations from ground-based geodetic stations. The recent development of the InSAR strapdown method suggests a solution to this problem. Yet, for an accurate decomposition, it is essential to isolate only scatterers representative of the deep gas-production-related deformation signal. Here we present a novel, data-driven approach that first disentangles the different deformation mechanisms present in the InSAR data. We then apply the strapdown method to decompose InSAR observations into vertical and directional horizontal displacement components, using frame orientation parameters estimated directly from the data. We incorporate uncontroversial contextual information and apply a bootstrapping method to enhance the quality of the results and propagate the uncertainty in the input data to provide quality metrics of the final estimates. Using this approach, we obtain reliable three-dimensional displacement estimates for the Groningen gas field, revealing previously unquantified horizontal displacements. Our results show that these horizontal displacements, especially close to the boundaries of the reservoir, are significant and must be considered alongside vertical motion to fully understand and mitigate the impacts of gas production.</jats:p>
title: 3D surface displacement estimation over the Groningen gas field, the Netherlands

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Boiler furnace temperature fields are significantly affected by strong nonlinearity and large time lags. Conventional methods exhibit limited capability in capturing spatiotemporal features and suffer from optimization delays, which restricts the efficient operation of boiler units.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To address this issue, this study proposes a multi-scale prediction method that combines a Lightweight Temporal Convolutional network with a Sequence-to-Sequence architecture. Wavelet packet decomposition is used to extract temperature sub-sequences, an encoding network is constructed, and a spatiotemporal dual attention mechanism is integrated to achieve accurate prediction of the furnace temperature field. In addition, a predictive control technique based on adaptive-reference-point multi-objective differential evolution is applied for combustion regulation. This technique takes multi-step prediction data as input, enhances collaborative optimization by introducing an adaptive update mechanism, and incorporates dual constraints on thermal efficiency and emissions to obtain the optimal control results.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      A 300 MW coal-fired utility boiler is selected as the research object for experimental validation. In furnace temperature prediction, the root mean square error of the proposed model is 1.53 °C, and the mean absolute percentage error under full load is 1.15%, both of which outperform those of baseline models. In control optimization experiments, the optimization time of the model is only 41.8 ms, and the fitness converges to 0.052. In the comprehensive validation, the proposed method reduces nitrogen oxide emissions to 175.2 mg/m
                      <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>
                      , increases thermal efficiency by 1.52%, suppresses steam temperature fluctuations within 1.7 °C, and limits the furnace negative pressure deviation to 10.5 Pa. All these indicators are better than those of similar techniques.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These results demonstrate the superior engineering performance and practical applicability of the proposed technique and provide support for efficient boiler combustion control.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Multi-scale predictive control of boiler furnace temperature field based on MPC-Seq2seq

items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study aims to analyse the interactions between sustainability reporting and social media communication, with particular attention to the actors involved, decision-making processes and strategies adopted to ensure effectiveness, consistency and transparency in sustainability communication.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study is based on a field study conducted in the Italian agri-food sector. Data were collected through 11 semi-structured interviews with managers responsible for sustainability reporting and/or corporate communication across nine Italian agri-food companies. The analysis is guided by an integrated theoretical framework combining communication theory and stakeholder theory.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Sustainability reports remain the central, validated repository of sustainability information, while social media are mainly used to amplify and adapt previously approved content. Stakeholder interactions on social media are monitored and managed but do not influence the content of sustainability reports. Sustainability managers act as gatekeepers of content validity and compliance, while social media managers translate information for platform-specific dissemination.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Social implications</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results highlight tensions among regulatory requirements, reputational risk and increasing expectations for transparency, raising questions about the actual dialogic potential of social media to foster accessible, inclusive sustainability communication.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study contributes to the sustainability accounting and communication literature by providing empirical evidence of limited informational circularity between sustainability reporting and social media. It advances an integrated explanation that links communication noise, stakeholder legitimacy considerations, organisational governance and regulatory pressures, thereby clarifying why the dialogic potential of social media remains constrained in practice. Finally, it highlights the interactions between the different actors involved in sustainability reporting disclosure.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Investigating the dynamics between sustainability reporting and social media. A field study

<jats:title>
                    A
                    <jats:sc>bstract</jats:sc>
                  </jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Within the known landscape of quantum gravity, most theories satisfy the Lattice Weak Gravity Conjecture (LWGC), which requires a superextremal particle at every site in the electric charge lattice Γ. However, counterexamples to the LWGC exist, and it was recently hypothesized that such counterexamples necessarily feature fractionally charged confined monopoles. In this work, we verify this hypothesis in toroidal orbifold compactifications of the heterotic string, which notably feature LWGC violation in both the abelian and nonabelian gauge sectors. In all the cases we consider, there exists a discrete subgroup of the center of the gauge group
                    <jats:italic>K</jats:italic>
                     ⊆ 
                    <jats:italic>Z</jats:italic>
                    (
                    <jats:italic>G</jats:italic>
                    ) such that superextremal particles exist at every site in the charge lattice of the quotient group
                    <jats:italic>G</jats:italic>
                    /
                    <jats:italic>K</jats:italic>
                    , while (confined) monopoles exist at all sites in the magnetic charge lattice of
                    <jats:italic>G</jats:italic>
                    /
                    <jats:italic>K</jats:italic>
                    . This suggests that LWGC violation cannot occur for gauge groups with trivial centers, and more generally the degree of LWGC violation in a nonabelian gauge theory is bounded in terms of the maximal order of the center.
                  </jats:p>
title: Nonabelian Lattice Weak Gravity Conjecture and monopole confinement

<jats:p>
                    Fluctuations of the three-dimensional (3-D) energy dissipation rate are very important in the study of intermittency in turbulence, but in experiments, often only one-dimensional (1-D) surrogates (the squared single velocity gradient component) are readily available. This work presents the mathematical derivation of a pair of transformation relations between the probability density functions (PDFs) of the 3-D dissipation and its 1-D surrogate for the case of incompressible isotropic turbulence where only five of six strain rate components are independent. It is shown that the left tails of the PDFs of the full dissipation and its 1-D surrogate obey power laws with the exponent
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" content-type="simple" xlink:href="S0022112026122460_inline1.png">
                          <jats:alt-text content-type="machine-generated">3 divided by 2</jats:alt-text>
                        </jats:inline-graphic>
                        <mml:math xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xmlns:mnf="http://cambridge.org/core/manifest" xmlns:cup="http://contentservices.cambridge.org" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:m="http://cambridge.org/core/metadata" xmlns:core="http://cambridge.org/core" xmlns:c="http://cambridge.org/core/content">
                          <mml:mn>3</mml:mn>
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mo>/</mml:mo>
                          </mml:mrow>
                          <mml:mn>2</mml:mn>
                        </mml:math>
                        <jats:tex-math>$3/2$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    and
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" content-type="simple" xlink:href="S0022112026122460_inline2.png">
                          <jats:alt-text content-type="machine-generated">negative 1 divided by 2</jats:alt-text>
                        </jats:inline-graphic>
                        <mml:math xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xmlns:mnf="http://cambridge.org/core/manifest" xmlns:cup="http://contentservices.cambridge.org" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:m="http://cambridge.org/core/metadata" xmlns:core="http://cambridge.org/core" xmlns:c="http://cambridge.org/core/content">
                          <mml:mo>−</mml:mo>
                          <mml:mn>1</mml:mn>
                          <mml:mrow>
                            <mml:mo>/</mml:mo>
                          </mml:mrow>
                          <mml:mn>2</mml:mn>
                        </mml:math>
                        <jats:tex-math>$-1/2$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    , respectively, similar to chi-square distributions of orders 5 and 1. The right tails are of the stretched-exponential form with the same stretched exponent which is smaller than unity. However, the decay rate of the tails of the 1-D surrogate is smaller, consistent with its being more intermittent than the 3-D dissipation. Alternative surrogate quantities defined from more than one velocity gradient show narrower tails in their PDFs. The theoretical results obtained require local isotropy, but are kinematic in nature and independent of Reynolds number. Normalised moments of the dissipation and its 1-D surrogate increase with Reynolds number, but their ratios depend on the order of the moment and are effectively Reynolds number independent. The theory is found to be in excellent agreement with two sources of direct numerical simulation data of forced isotropic turbulence with Taylor-scale Reynolds number ranging from 360 to 2500.
                  </jats:p>
title: Probability density functions of energy dissipation and one-dimensional surrogate in isotropic turbulence

items.abstract: <jats:p>Vibration and coil-current signals provide complementary information on the mechanical condition of high-voltage circuit breaker operating mechanisms. This study experimentally evaluates a specific compact workflow using feature-level fusion on a 40.5 kV outdoor vacuum circuit breaker under normal operation, bolt loosening, opening-spring force degradation, and non-latching closure. Signal-specific preprocessing uses variational mode decomposition (VMD)-assisted wavelet soft-threshold denoising for vibration and direct wavelet soft-threshold denoising for coil current. Box dimensions of local mean decomposition (LMD) component power spectra and closing-coil current timing and amplitude descriptors are fused, reduced by principal component analysis, and classified using K-nearest neighbors. The fused model correctly identifies 117 of 120 test samples (97.50%), compared with 87.50% for vibration alone, 90.00% for current alone, and 90.83% without dimensionality reduction. These results support the selected representation for the evaluated breaker, four conditions, and reported test partition under controlled no-load operation. Validation on independent breakers and under field conditions is needed before broader application.</jats:p>
title: Vibration and Coil-Current Fusion for Mechanical Fault Diagnosis of High-Voltage Circuit Breaker Operating Mechanisms

                  <jats:p>
                    First law consistency alone does not determine the black hole state space of NUT-charged spacetimes, because several inequivalent macroscopic formulations can yield consistent thermodynamics. We develop a two-horizon sector diagnostic for the electrically charged Kerr-Newman-NUT family by organizing the inner- and outer-horizon entropies and inverse temperatures into sum (Σ) and difference (∆) sectors. The charged rotating geometry gives a more stringent test of the uncharged Taub-NUT sector result, since the mass
                    <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                    , ordinary electric charge
                    <jats:italic>Q</jats:italic>
                    , ordinary angular momentum
                    <jats:italic>J</jats:italic>
                    , NUT charge
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                    , and the NUT secondary hair
                    <jats:italic>J</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    =
                    <jats:italic>MN</jats:italic>
                    all enter the same two-horizon thermodynamics. For the physically anchored minimal homogeneous state spaces defined and tested here, we find a clear sector separation: the Σ sector closes with the charge-like variables
                    <jats:italic>Q</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                    , whereas the ∆ sector additionally requires the rotation-like variables
                    <jats:italic>J</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>J</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    . Natural reductions that eliminate either
                    <jats:italic>J</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    or
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                    fail to reproduce the first law coefficient fixed by the sector temperature, and their associated Bekenstein-Smarr relations do not close with the assigned scaling weights. Within this class, electric charge and ordinary rotation therefore do not absorb the NUT secondary response, and the charged rotating family supports the NUT bi-hair organization:
                    <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>

                    =

items.abstract: <jats:p>The Research Center for High-Value Recycling of Emerging Solid Wastes (RC-HRESW) at the Guangzhou Institute of Energy Conversion focuses on the circular utilization of retired new-energy devices, thereby contributing to China’s energy transition and resource sustainability, and supporting its carbon-neutrality goals. Building on a thermochemical deconstruction-reconstruction framework for organic solid wastes, the Center has developed full-chain technologies covering intelligent dismantling, clean thermochemical conversion, and high-quality metal recovery. This article summarizes the Center’s recent advances in the recycling of retired new-energy devices, together with over 20 engineering demonstration projects for solid waste recycling. By integrating fundamental research, key technologies, large-scale demonstration, and major infrastructure projects, the Center is striving to establish a circular new-energy system and to provide scalable solutions for clean, low-carbon development.</jats:p>
title: Safeguarding the Last Mile in the Transition to New Energy: Innovations in High-Value Recycling of Retired New-energy Devices

<jats:p>
                    The growing necessity to create efficient and sustainable energy systems has also promoted the development of the high‐performance supercapacitors having better energy and power densities. This study prepared NiSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ‐graphene oxide (NiSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ‐GO) nanocomposites through a hydrothermal process and investigated them as electrode materials in asymmetric supercapacitors. GO incorporation greatly increased the electrical conductivity, ion‐diffusion kinetics, and structural stability of NiSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    , and this helps to improve the charge‐storage behavior. Electrochemical studies were used to confirm the presence of both the pseudocapacitative and the electric double‐layer mechanisms in the composite material. The NiSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ‐GO electrode showed a remarkable specific capacitance of 830 F g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    at a scan rate of 5 mVs
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    , which is an indication of its great capacity to hold charges. A particular capacitance of 115 F g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    at 1 A g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    was obtained when packaged into NiSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ‐GO//AC asymmetric and an energy density of 18 Wh/kg and a power density of 1800 W/kg were obtained. Furthermore, the device was very stable during cycling with 92% Coulombic efficiency intact even at 10 000 charge–discharge cycles. The exceptional efficiency of the NiSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ‐GO nanocomposite can be explained by the synergistic effect of the pseudocapacitive NiSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    and highly conducting GO, which provides high speeds of electron flow and steadiness of ion diffusion across the electrode set up. These findings indicate that NiSe
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ‐GO nanocomposites have a high potential as the ideal candidates of the next‐generation high‐performance and long‐lasting supercapacitor electrodes.
                  </jats:p>
title:
Interfacial Coupling in NiSe
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    ‐GO Hybrids Enables High‐Performance and Stable Energy Storage

items.abstract: <jats:p>In this note we report data on autumn-winter roosting density and behaviour of Spotless Starling (Sturnus unicolor), a poorly studied species of high biogeographic interest, carried out in a small urban town of northern Sardinia (Bonorva, Sassari). Spotless Starlings were recorded between October 2021 and February 2022 (n=4,272), with a maximum number of records in November (mean values: >800 ind./km), significantly decreasing until February. Compared to trees, buildings appear to represent privileged perching sites (contrary to what is known for the Common Starling, Sturnus vulgaris): they were probably selected for the higher temperatures and for the absence of nocturnal predators. Although metal deterrents traditionally used for pigeons have been installed on some buildings locally, the smaller starlings still settle between the steel spikes, partly due to their ability to perch on very small surfaces. Given the ineffectiveness of theseanti-perching devices, it will be important to modify the distance, density and inclination of the steel tips (originally defined for pigeons) to adapt them to the size and behavior of Spotless Starlings or creatively develop alternative and non-lethal solutions to limit the number of these birds creating conflicts with citizens.</jats:p>
title: Spotless Starling (<i>Sturnus unicolor</i>) in a Sardinian town (Italy): mechanical anti-perching deterrents are not effective in high density roosts

items.abstract: <jats:p>The experiment was carried out to examine the performance of paired-row pigeonpea in a high-density cotton intercropping system and to evaluate the quality and economics of high-density cotton grown with paired-row pigeonpea. The space between the two paired rows of pigeonpea was effectively used to grow high-density cotton. The trial was conducted at the Agricultural Research Station (ARS) Tandur, Vikarabad during kharif 2023–24 and 2024–25 and was laid out in a split-plot design with 3 replications. The main plots comprised paired rows of pigeonpea between high-density cotton spacing, while the subplots consisted of 6 treatments with varying levels of nitrogen and growth regulators. Among the main plots, the high-density cotton spacing of 60 × 15 cm (M1) significantly recorded the highest mean maximum gross returns (243347), net returns and benefit–cost (B : C) ratio (2.68), as well as land equivalent ratio (LER) of (1.36). However, the superior fibre quality parameters were observed with the higher density cotton spacing of 100 × 15 cm (M3) during 2023–24, 2024–25 and in the mean results. Among the subplots, the highest mean gross returns (243589), net returns (155015), B : C ratio (2.74) and LER of (1.38) were recorded and the maximum quality parameters were obtained with the application of 125 % recommended dose of nitrogen (RDN) + mepiquat chloride 50 ppm at the square formation and flowering stage (S3). This treatment was statistically comparable to the application of 100 % RDN + mepiquat chloride 50 ppm at the square formation and flowering stage (S2), which produced mean gross returns (213855), net returns (136907), B : C ratio (2.55) and LER of (1.31). The application of 125 % RDN + cycocel 60 ppm at the square formation and flowering stage (S6) also showed comparable performance, with mean gross returns (227144), net returns (138970), B : C ratio (2.57) and LER of 1.28 across 2023–24, 2024–25 and the mean data.</jats:p>
title: Quality, land-use efficiency and economics of  high-density cotton in paired-row pigeonpea intercropping under different nitrogen and growth regulator management

                    <jats:sc>bstract</jats:sc>

                  <jats:p>
                    We construct cubic scalar field theory on
                    <jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>
                    -Minkowski space by combining the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism with harmonic analysis, and produce two inequivalent noncommutative quantum field theories. The braided theory is based on a braided
                    <jats:italic>L</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>∞</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    -algebra whereby covariance dictates a spectral decomposition into cylindrical Bessel functions that diagonalise the angular Drinfel’d twist; in this theory we find the usual logarithmic ultraviolet divergences and confirm the absence of UV/IR mixing. The standard noncommutative theory is based on a classical
                    <jats:italic>L</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>
                      <jats:italic>∞</jats:italic>
                    </jats:sub>
                    -algebra; in this theory we relate the spectral decompositions into plane wave and cylindrical harmonic eigenmodes of the Klein-Gordan operator, we verify the planar equivalence theorem, and we demonstrate a periodic form of UV/IR mixing in which non-planar correlators are generically ultraviolet finite but become non-analytic on an infinite lattice of exceptional momenta.
                  </jats:p>
title: Batalin-Vilkovisky quantization with an angular twist

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We propose a model, consisting of an Long Short‐Term Memory Encoder‐Decoder backbone along with a novel late dynamic fusion mechanism for adaptively integrating learned representations from multisource hydrometeorological data for 7‐day‐ahead streamflow forecasting. This model is applied to both univariate (single‐flow gauge) and multivariate (multi‐gauge) streamflow forecasting in Severn Basin (UK), known for prolonged medium‐to high‐flow periods. Results show that the proposed dynamic fusion approach exceeded the attention‐based fusion, with an average improvement of 5.54% in Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and 3.55% in  for overall and high‐flow accuracy. Furthermore, the proposed approach outperforms traditional machine‐learning baselines, lowering overall MAE by up to 12.1% and high‐flow errors by up to 16.8%. Additionally, multivariate models are significantly faster in both training and inference by 76% and yield comparable accuracy to univariate models, but uncertainty analysis reveals that are more sensitive to the high‐flows than the latter. Overall, the model achieved a Nash‐Sutcliffe Efficiency of 0.76. Finally, the use of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (KernelSHAP) confirmed the dominant role of precipitation, past river flows, and the most recent timesteps in the underlying hydrologic process.</jats:p>
title: High‐Flow Forecasting With a Deep Learning‐Based Dynamic Feature Fusion Approach

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Precision and compliance are essential to high-contact robotic tasks, while contact oscillations can be vital to both the end effector as well as the operation object. Passivity-based energy regulation of robot manipulators is a promising way to maintain decent operation behavior. However, current passive admittance methods in Cartesian-space depend on accurate pose reconstruction, making them difficult to apply directly to vision-guided high-precision alignment tasks. Furthermore, conventional passivity-based control usually requires large damping or strong energy constraints, leading to conservative control behavior. To address these limitations, a three-layer dynamic model consisting of nominal, offset and measured states is constructed, and a bidirectional energy-flow modulation mechanism is introduced to adaptively regulate energy exchange according to the real-time status. Moreover, a PID-based energy compensation, an adaptive virtual damping and an energy tank mechanism are integrated to constrain energy injection, dissipation, and release, thereby ensuring closed-loop passivity preservation while maintaining dynamic performances. Bolt alignment experiments are conducted under different initial positions, tilt-angle deviations and strong-contact conditions. At initial position 1, compared with shear thickening fluid visual admittance method, the proposed method reduces the peak contact force to 19.21 N, shortens the alignment time to 6.11 s, and decreases the residual contact force after alignment to 0.73 N, corresponding to reductions of 65.4%, 39.14%, and 81.09%. At the more challenging initial position 2, it still completes stable alignment with a minimum peak force of 5.58 N and the shortest time of 6.04 s. These results demonstrate improved impact suppression, dynamic response, task efficiency and reduced conservativeness.</jats:p>
title: Bidirectional energy-flow modulation for passive visual admittance control using vision–force measurement fusion

<jats:p>
                    The process of change of the surface structures of the Pb/Mo (110) system is discussed on the basis of the reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) analysis results. The appearance of the (10×4), (2×3), (2×10), and (3×2) structures is confirmed, and the (2×3) and (2×10) structures are confirmed to possess other mirror structures with respect to the [1-10]
                    <jats:sub>Mo</jats:sub>
                    direction. The (10×4) structure maintains a nearly regular trianglular configuration, similar to the atomic arrangement along the Pb (111) plane. Regarding the (2×3), (2×10), and (3×2) structures, their features commonly indicate the line coincidence along both the [1-11] and [1-1-1] directions.
                  </jats:p>
title: Symmetrical Phase Transition of Pb/Mo(110) System Investigated by Reflection High-Energy Electron Diffraction

items.abstract: <jats:p>Repeated tree rows and foliage occlusion make stereo feature tracking difficult in orchards, especially when a robot alternates between slow motion and brief stops. We introduce two observation-dependent mechanisms into VINS-Fusion. The first uses the median Sampson distance from mature stereo tracks to choose once between fixed and online camera–IMU extrinsic estimation. The second evaluates angular velocity, gravity-compensated acceleration, optical-flow hysteresis and pre-update velocity before adding a zero-velocity residual to the newest velocity state. We evaluated the implementation on eight EuRoC and three orchard sequences. On Wampee and Mango, adaptive selection produced three-run mean APE-RMSE values within 0.6% of the fixed-extrinsic baseline. Relative to online estimation, paired-run aggregate APE-RMSE decreased by 19.94% with adaptive selection and by 20.32% with the complete method. On EuRoC, the changes were +0.81% across eight sequences and −2.46% across five sequences, respectively. The effect of the zero-velocity constraint varied between sequences. These results suggest that using stereo geometric evidence to choose an extrinsic configuration can help avoid unfavorable online calibration in the orchard conditions examined.</jats:p>
title: Geometry-Guided Extrinsic Model Selection and Motion-Gated Constraints for Stereo Visual–Inertial Estimation in Orchards

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The growing demand for environmentally sustainable alternatives in the development of carbon‐based reinforced polymer composites has driven researchers to explore additives derived from renewable natural resources. In this study, agricultural olive waste was converted to a carbonaceous material through pyrolysis and utilized as reinforcement in high‐density polyethylene. The produced composite specimens were characterized with respect to their morphological characteristics and thermomechanical properties. The acquired experimental data were used to develop a continuum mechanical model, employing an inverse homogenization approach, to estimate the elastic properties of the biochar reinforcements. The predicted mechanical properties of the latter were found to be in good agreement with the experimental results for composite specimens with different volume fractions, demonstrating the synergies between experimental and
                    <jats:italic>in silico</jats:italic>
                    approaches in the development of circular composites. Overall, this work promotes waste valorization of olive tree pruning residues – an abundant Mediterranean agricultural waste – into functional biochar fillers of polymer composites. The findings highlight a strong dependence of the mechanical performance of the composites on filler activation, concentration and uniform dispersion. An integrated experimental–computational framework is demonstrated for its potential to elucidate the mechanics of the microstructural environment that will accelerate the rational design of next‐generation sustainable composites. © 2026 The Author(s).
                    <jats:italic>Polymer International</jats:italic>
                    published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of Society of Chemical Industry.
                  </jats:p>
title: Olive waste biochar‐reinforced high‐density polyethylene composites

items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Multimodal deep learning for glaucoma detection often combines fundus imaging with optical coherence tomography (OCT), yet it is unclear when fusion adds information beyond OCT alone and how such models behave under domain shift. We compared joint and late fusion of scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO) and OCT and their cross-domain transfer. Methods: Models trained on GAMMA (color fundus photographs and macular OCT; 99 cases) were applied without retraining to the Harvard-FairVision glaucoma test split (3000 patients; SLO and OCT). Unimodal and multimodal models were then trained on FairVision (6000 training and 1000 validation patients). Four candidates (OCT-only, concatenation and cross-attention fusion, and late fusion with a cross-fitted SLO weight of 0.15) were locked with their calibration and thresholds and evaluated once on the same test split. Results: Cross-domain transfer yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) of 0.635–0.653. In-domain OCT-only reached a test AUROC of 0.876. Neither jointly trained cross-attention fusion (ΔAUROC −0.0045; 95% confidence interval (CI) −0.0110 to 0.0021) nor concatenation fusion (+0.0009; 95% CI −0.0056 to 0.0074) improved on OCT-only. Late fusion yielded a small ranking improvement (+0.0059; 95% CI 0.0033 to 0.0087; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0012), but a sensitivity gain at matched specificity was not established. Post hoc analyses identified lower AUROC among Black patients and a higher false-positive rate among normal eyes. Conclusions: OCT carried most of the diagnostic information. Standard joint fusion did not add value. Low-weight late fusion improved ranking slightly on a previously accessed test split; this requires independent confirmation and does not establish clinical benefit. Fusion claims require strong unimodal and late-fusion baselines and external validation.</jats:p>
title: When Does Multimodal Fusion Help? Cross-Domain Transfer, Joint Fusion, and Late Fusion of SLO and OCT for Glaucoma Detection Under an Analysis-Locked Evaluation

<jats:p>
                    Adipose tissue must remain mechanically adaptable to accommodate continued lipid storage, but whether this capacity can be limited by a persistent external mechanical constraint remains unclear. We hypothesize that sustained external abdominal confinement can oppose deformation and expansion of established abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue, thereby reducing its regional capacity for further lipid storage. This differs from impaired expandability caused by fibrosis, defective adipogenesis, or intrinsic abnormalities in adipocyte mechanoadaptation, in that the proposed constraint is imposed at the tissue boundary. Recent studies showing that adipocyte hypertrophy requires plasma-membrane and cytoskeletal remodeling provide a mechanobiological basis for this possibility. We further predict that the response will depend on both loading magnitude and duration: mild restriction may remain reversible, sustained non-injurious confinement may limit tissue and adipocyte expansion, whereas excessive loading may instead produce inflammatory or injurious responses. As preliminary context, secondary analysis of a published dataset comparing mature adipocytes with polyethylene glycol (PEG)-induced dedifferentiated adipocytes showed lower adipogenesis, fatty acid metabolism, and mature-adipocyte transcriptional programs. In an independent intact-tissue experiment, adipose tissue maintained in mechanically distinct gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) environments differed in apparent Young’s modulus and in expression of
                    <jats:italic>Pparg</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic>Nr1h3</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic>Acaca</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic>Acox1</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic>Cpt1a</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>Ppara</jats:italic>
                    . These observations neither reproduce circumferential abdominal confinement nor demonstrate restricted adipocyte hypertrophy, reduced adipose mass or fat loss. Rather, they provide a basis for testing whether sustained external restriction can limit regional adipose expandability. Any reduction in expansion of a constrained depot must also be distinguished from true loss of body fat because lipid-storage demand may instead be redistributed to other adipose depots or ectopic tissues.
                  </jats:p>
title: Sustained external abdominal confinement as a mechanical constraint on adipose tissue expandability

items.abstract: <jats:p>Spin-1/2 Sn isotopes are intriguing prospects for nuclear spin-based universal quantum computation platforms, in which long-distance, inter-nuclear, two-qubit operations are mediated by an electron-shuttling mechanism. Here, we report progress toward device fabrication for this platform by blanket ion implantation. In the silicon metal–oxide–semiconductor system of interest, we find a Sn implant fluence of 4.3×1013 cm−2 and a post-implant anneal at 900 °C will produce a balance between maximizing Sn count in the substrate and minimizing interface damage, with the latter quantified here by the interface state density (Dit). A Sn concentration near the Si solubility limit is achieved around 5 nm from the Si/SiO2 interface using an 18 keV accelerating voltage for the Sn implant, and Si recrystallization is nearly complete after a 750 °C anneal. A minimum Dit is maintained for 900–1000 °C post-implant anneals but significantly increases at higher anneal temperatures. This work highlights favorable processing conditions toward the technological viability of integrating Sn nuclear spin qubits in a Si host with electron spin qubits.</jats:p>
title: Interface state density minimization in tin implanted silicon toward quantum dot-coupled tin qubits

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Neuroepithelial tumors with PLAGL1 fusion represent a recently defined methylation class characterized by distinctive epigenetic features and frequent histopathological features consistent with ependymal differentiation, predominantly affecting young children. Different fusion partners have been described, most commonly EWSR1 and FOXO1, but their biological impact remains poorly understood. Further molecular insights from this rare entity are needed to deeper understand the heterogeneous spectrum of fusion-positive neuroepithelial tumors.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Bulk RNA sequencing was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded samples of supratentorial ependymoma-like tumors lacking ZFTA or YAP1 fusions. Transcriptional profiles were analyzed in tumors harboring PLAGL1 fusions. Differential expression (DE) analysis and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) were performed, including comparisons with reference cohorts of ZFTA and YAP1 fusion-positive supratentorial ependymomas to identify fusion-specific transcriptional programs. DNA methylation profiling was used for tumor classification and clustering.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this retrospective cohort, PLAGL1 fusion was identified in 22 tumors, including EWSR1::PLAGL1 (n = 16) and PLAGL1::FOXO1 (n = 6). Dimensionality reduction analyses showed distinct clustering both at the epigenetic and the transcriptomic levels according to fusion partner. EWSR1::PLAGL1 tumors showed a strong activation of progenitor/mesenchymal-like programs, with high expression of homeobox genes HOXD3 and HOXD8. GSEA analysis revealed enriched oxidative phosphorylation compared to PLAGL1::FOXO1 tumors, with increased expression of the mitochondrial regulator PPARGC1A. In contrast, PLAGL1::FOXO1 tumors displayed a more pronounced astro-glial differentiation, with an enrichment of ciliogenesis-related pathways and elevated GFAP expression. These tumors also showed increased expression of MTOR, suggesting potential involvement of mTOR signaling.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Neuroepithelial tumors with PLAGL1 fusion are biologically heterogeneous and exhibit fusion partner-specific developmental and metabolic states. EWSR1::PLAGL1 tumors are characterized by a HOXD-associated developmental activation and metabolic reprogramming, whereas PLAGL1::FOXO1 tumors display a more differentiated transcriptional phenotype. These findings support the existence of distinct biological states within the PLAGL1-fusion spectrum and warrant further investigation for refined classification and potential therapeutic targeting. Ongoing studies aim to correlate these molecular features with clinicopathological characteristics.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: P14.06.B Fusion partner drives developmental and metabolic divergence in ependymoma-like neuroepithelial tumors with PLAGL1 fusion

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Compared with ring laser gyro, fiber optic gyro (FOG) have two inherent performance defects: poor start-up temperature characteristics and poor scale factor error repeatability. Both defects will degrade the heading angle alignment accuracy of the rotational fiber optic inertial navigation system (INS) when conventional self-alignment schemes are adopted. Previous studies mainly focused on improving alignment schemes to reduce the impact of only one of the two FOG defects on self-alignment accuracy. However, in practical engineering applications, these two defects of FOGs exhibit a synergistic effect, synchronously introducing heading angle alignment errors into the rotational fiber optic INS. To address this issue, this paper analyzes the underlying mathematical mechanism of this phenomenon. On the basis of inheriting the advantages of the conventional two-position and continuous rotation alignment methods, a novel two-position rotation self-alignment scheme is proposed. By designing a reasonable indexing scheme, the filtering estimation error of the azimuth misalignment angle during the rotation process is offset against the attitude tracking error caused by indexing, thereby synchronously suppressing the heading angle alignment errors introduced by the FOG scale factor error and start-up temperature characteristics. The high and low temperature alignment test data show that the alignment accuracy of the two-position rotation alignment method is improved by approximately 35″ and 86″ relative to the former two schemes, respectively.</jats:p>
title: A two-position rotation alignment scheme for rotational fiber optic inertial navigation system

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Silver‐based catalysts have attracted extensive research interest for the electrochemical CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    reduction reaction (CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    RR). However, their selectivity is typically limited to CO due to the inherently weak binding strength with the
                    <jats:sup>*</jats:sup>
                    CO intermediate. Here, we develop a catalyst of ultrafine silver nanoclusters confined within nitrogen‐doped mesoporous carbon (Ag‐in) via a pore‐confinement strategy for efficient electrochemical CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ‐to‐ethanol conversion. The Ag‐in catalyst achieves a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 15.3% for ethanol at −1.25 V vs. RHE in a flow cell, with a production rate of 99.4 µmol h
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    . In contrast, the control catalyst with silver nanoparticles supported predominantly on the exterior surface of the mesoporous carbon (Ag‐out) shows no detectable ethanol production during CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    RR. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that this unique selectivity arises from the low‐coordinated silver nanoclusters with an increased d‐band center and enhanced *CO binding affinity, along with the promoted CO concentration in the vicinity of Ag catalytic sites due to the confinement effect of mesoporous carbon. This work not only presents a novel approach for efficient ethanol production from electrochemical CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    RR but also paves the way for the development of non‐copper‐based catalysts for carbon‐neutral energy conversion processes.
                  </jats:p>
title:
Pore‐Confined Ag Nanoclusters for Electrochemical CO
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Reduction to Ethanol via Enhanced CO Binding and Intermediate Confinement

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)-based electrolytes suffer from sluggish Li-ion transport and insufficient interfacial stability toward the lithium anode. Herein, we introduce fructone (ethyl 2-(2-methyl-1,3-dioxolan-2-yl)acetate, EMDA), a commercially available and environmentally benign small molecule, as a multifunctional regulator for simultaneously improving bulk ion transport and lithium-anode interfacial stability. The rigid cyclic framework of EMDA disrupts the ordered packing of PEO chains, reducing polymer crystallinity while maintaining mechanical robustness. Meanwhile, its electron-rich ester and ether oxygen atoms of EMDA participate in competitive Li-ion coordination, alleviating the strong coordination of Li ions with PEO chains. In addition, EMDA preferentially participates in interfacial reactions during cycling, promoting the formation of a Li2O-rich solid electrolyte interphase that facilitates uniform lithium deposition and suppresses dendrite growth. Benefiting from the synergistic regulation, the optimized PEO–EMDA solid polymer electrolyte Li||Li symmetric cells exhibit stable cycling for more than 1300 h, whereas Li||LiFePO4 full cells retain 95.6% of their initial capacity retention after 300 cycles. This work demonstrates an effective molecular-regulation strategy for simultaneously optimizing ion transport and interfacial stability in solid polymer batteries.</jats:p>
title: A Multifunctional Molecular Regulator Enables Fast Ion Transport and a Li2O-Rich Interphase for High-Performance Solid-State Lithium Batteries

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The power conversion efficiency (PCE) of small-area organic solar cells (OSCs) has now exceeded 20%. However, most high-performance devices are still fabricated by using halogenated solvents, whose toxicity limits industrial-scale production. In this study, a facile ternary nonhalogenated solvent strategy is developed, consisting of ortho-xylene (o-XY, boiling point (BP): 144.4 °C), toluene (TOL, BP: 110 °C), and carbon disulfide (CS2, BP: 46.2 °C). Through comprehensive optimization of the solvent ratio, this strategy enables optimization of solvent evaporation kinetics, thereby governing film formation dynamics and nanoscale molecular orientation. As a result, large-scale phase separation is effectively suppressed while highly uniform large-area active layers are obtained. Based on this ternary solvent strategy, nonhalogenated solvent-processed OSCs and large-area organic solar modules (with an active area of 12 cm2) based on PM6:L8-BO:BTP-eC9 achieve PCEs of 18.7% and 16.2%, respectively. The ternary nonhalogenated solvent strategy provides a viable pathway to develop high-performance large-area organic solar modules.</jats:p>
title: High-Efficiency Large-Area Organic Solar Modules Enabled by a Ternary Nonhalogenated Solvent Strategy

items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As micro‐light‐emitting diodes are reduced to below 10 µm, conventional transfer and assembly methods cannot meet the accuracy and yield required for next‐generation high‐resolution, low‐cost displays. To overcome these limitations, we previously proposed a face‐selective dielectrophoresis (FS‐DEP) method for the vertical assembly of fin‐Light‐emitting diodes (fin‐LEDs) that enables vertical electroluminescence. However, the conventional FS‐DEP process is still impeded by misalignment due to rail‐like sliding between the electrodes during assembly. In this study, we present a central‐focused dielectrophoresis (CF‐DEP) assembly strategy that utilizes dielectric‐guided barrier lines on the electrodes. These structures create dual‐gradient confinement forces at four key points: the edges of the electrodes and the tops of the dielectric barriers. By spatially confining electric field gradients, this configuration induces self‐centering of the fin‐LEDs and effectively prevents vertical sliding. The results of CF‐DEP show that this method significantly improves the yield and assembly precision of p‐GaN contacts while minimizing issues such as aggregation, overlap, and tilting. These improvements were attained through systematic optimization of barrier materials, geometric design, and parameters related to DEP voltage and frequency, all supported by simulations using COMSOL. The proposed approach offers a scalable, high‐precision solution for integrating fin‐LEDs into large‐area displays that will advance next‐generation nano/micro‐LED technologies.</jats:p>
title: Central‐Focused Dielectrophoretic Assembly of Fin‐LEDs via Guided Barrier Line‐Assisted Dual‐Gradient Confinement

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Breast ultrasound (BUS) is widely used in breast imaging because it is non-ionizing and well suited to dense breast tissue. However, speckle noise, blurry mass boundaries, and large variations in lesion scale remain challenging for automated segmentation. This paper presents GMR-EfficientUNet, an EfficientNet-B2/U-Net-based encoder-decoder framework that adapts a Gated Bottleneck Convolution (GBC) module and a Multi-Scale Convolutional Attention (MSCA) module from prior work and combines them with a Residual Adaptive Fusion (RAF) module for breast ultrasound mass segmentation. Within the proposed integration, GBC is applied to refine the initially fused encoder-decoder representation, MSCA performs multi-scale contextual modeling on the refined features, and RAF learns pixel-level fusion weights between the enhanced representation and the original DoubleConv feature. On the BUSI dataset, the model achieved a Dice coefficient of 82.07%, MIoU of 73.73%, recall of 83.49%, and precision of 83.62%. On the BUET dataset, it achieved a Dice coefficient of 81.70% and MIoU of 72.57%; among the evaluated models, it obtained the highest Dice, MIoU, and recall, while TransUNet achieved a higher precision. The ablation results demonstrated the effectiveness of RAF in improving segmentation performance. Additional experiments showed improved boundary localization, competitive performance against alternative fusion strategies, and consistent Dice improvements across five training runs.</jats:p>
title: GMR-EfficientUNet: an improved network integrating gated bottleneck convolution and multi-scale attention residual fusion for high-precision breast ultrasound mass segmentation

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We present a new computational approach based on Nuclear-Electronic Orbital and Subsystem Density Functional Theory. The resulting NEO-sDFT methodology enables quantum chemical calculations of large molecular systems composed of thousands of atoms while also describing selected protons quantum mechanically. A key feature of the associated program implementation is its flexibility in assigning quantum protons to subsystems, allowing different embedding schemes to be employed within a unified framework. The accuracy of NEO-sDFT is assessed by computing energies of water clusters of growing size. Deviations from reference Nuclear-Electronic Orbital Density Functional Theory results amount to only a few meV for water dimers near the equilibrium separation and are comparable to those of conventional Subsystem Density Functional Theory for larger clusters. The favorable computational scaling of NEO-sDFT is further showcased through calculations on water clusters of increasing size, with up to 303 protons being treated quantum mechanically. Our results demonstrate that NEO-sDFT is an accurate and efficient approach for incorporating nuclear quantum effects into large-scale simulations, providing a foundation for future applications to proton transfer processes in biochemical systems.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates spatial segregation in "swarm" sounds, a class of auditory textures arising from multiples of rhythmic sound elements modeled on collective swarm dynamics in nature. Such sounds provide a controlled framework, inspired by naturally occurring textures, for exploring how rhythmic signals can be detected within dense auditory textures. Using ensembles of metronomes to approximate such swarms, we examined how density and spatial separation affect listeners' ability to detect and synchronize with an embedded target rhythm. Thirteen participants tapped along with a target metronome presented at varying azimuthal angles (0° to 65°) relative to a swarm masker directly ahead, with density varied across ten levels (200 to 920 sources). Detection probability increased with angular separation and decreased with swarm density, with a significant detection interaction suggesting that denser textures expand the spatial masking region. At low densities, reliable detection occurred at approximately 21°, while higher densities required separations of 29° or greater. Synchronization accuracy, measured via normalized inter-tap intervals, was reduced near the detection threshold, and reaction times increased under challenging spatial conditions. In general, the findings indicate that spatial position and source density jointly shape the extent to which rhythmic targets can be detected by sensorimotor synchronization.</jats:p>
title: Detecting Rhythmic Signals in "Swarm" Auditory Textures: Effects of Source Position, Density, and Synchronization Ability

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In this work, a 3D CoFe-Prussian blue analogue (PBA) nanocube was synthesized via coprecipitation and subsequently assembled onto single-layer Ti3C2Tx MXene (MX/MXene) using a freeze-drying-assisted ex situ solution-mixing approach to obtain a CoFe-PBA/MXene composite for high-performance energy storage applications. The structural and morphological features of the prepared materials were systematically analyzed using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman spectroscopy, Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface area analysis, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), field emission scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (FESEM-EDX), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The electrochemical performance of CoFe-PBA, MXene, CoFe-PBA@MX-10 wt %, CoFe-PBA@MX-20 wt %, and CoFe-PBA@MX-30 wt % electrodes were evaluated in 3 M KOH electrolyte. Among them, the CoFe-PBA@MX-20 wt % composite exhibited excellent electrochemical performance, with a high specific capacitance of 1010 F g–1 at 1 A g–1 in a half-cell system. Furthermore, an asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) device was fabricated using CoFe-PBA@MX-20 wt % as the cathode material and activated carbon as the anode material. The assembled device exhibits a specific capacitance of 122.58 F g–1, with an energy storage capability of 40.9 Wh kg–1 and a power capability of 775 W kg–1. In addition, the device exhibits excellent cycling stability with 93.4% capacitance retention and 99.5% coulombic efficiency after 5000 cycles at 1 A g–1. These results suggest that the CoFe-PBA@MX-20 wt % composite is a promising electrode material for an advanced high-energy storage device.</jats:p>
title: Hierarchical 3D CoFe-Prussian Blue Analogue Nanocubes Anchored on Single-Layer Ti3C2T x MXene Sheets for High-Performance Pseudocapacitive Energy Storage
