items.abstract: <jats:p>Seleksi fitur merupakan tahap penting dalam meningkatkan kinerja dan interpretabilitas model machine learning pada diagnosis kanker kolorektal, terutama dalam menangani data medis berdimensi tinggi. Penelitian ini menyajikan kajian komprehensif mengenai penerapan seleksi fitur pada diagnosis kanker kolorektal berbasis machine learning melalui pendekatan terintegrasi Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dan analisis bibliometrik. Sebanyak 53 artikel yang dipublikasikan pada periode 2020–2025 dikumpulkan dari database Scopus dan diseleksi menggunakan pedoman PRISMA. Analisis bibliometrik dilakukan dengan bantuan perangkat lunak VOSviewer untuk mengidentifikasi tren publikasi, struktur konseptual, dan evolusi topik penelitian, sementara SLR digunakan untuk mengkaji metode seleksi fitur, algoritma machine learning, serta tujuan dan temuan utama setiap studi. Hasil analisis menunjukkan empat klaster penelitian utama, yaitu analisis biomarker dan data pasien kanker kolorektal, seleksi fitur berbasis optimasi, interpretabilitas model dan feature importance, serta penerapan deep learning pada citra histopatologi. Meskipun metode seleksi fitur berbasis optimasi seperti Genetic Algorithm dan Particle Swarm Optimization mendominasi penelitian, namun seleksi firur yang menggabungkan Genetic Algorithm dan Particle Swarm Optimization belum terlihat. Kebaruan penelitian ini terletak pada pemetaan terintegrasi lintas klaster yang secara eksplisit mengungkap kesenjangan antara performa komputasional dan kesiapan klinis, serta memberikan arah pengembangan seleksi fitur hibrida dan interpretable untuk diagnosis kanker kolorektal di masa depan.</jats:p>
title: Seleksi Fitur pada Diagnosis Kanker Kolorektal Berbasis Machine Learning: SLR dan Bibliometrik

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Soil salinity is a major challenge for sustainable agricultural production, particularly in irrigated regions, where repeated soil surveys are costly and often unavailable. This study explored whether legacy soil physicochemical data could be used to support soil salinity assessment under data-scarce conditions by integrating them with Sentinel-2 imagery and machine learning. Ridge Regression (RR) and Support Vector Regression (SVR) models were developed using soil properties and Sentinel-2-derived salinity indices from 2015. To determine whether reducing the number of predictors could improve model performance, models were built using both the complete dataset (CDS) and a reduced dataset (RDS) obtained through Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE). Ridge Regression consistently performed better than SVR, and the RDS achieved the highest prediction accuracy (R² = 0.99, RMSE = 2.652, NRMSE = 0.034, and MAE = 1.891). The optimized RR model was then applied using salinity indices derived from Sentinel-2 imagery acquired in 2022 to examine whether a model calibrated with legacy soil information could still be applied when contemporary EC measurements were not available. Although the model maintained high predictive performance, the 2022 salinity indices showed no significant relationship with the measured EC. A similar result was obtained for NDVI, which was also not significantly correlated with the EC. These results indicate that the model performance was largely controlled by the legacy soil physicochemical properties, whereas the contemporary spectral indices contributed little to explaining soil salinity under the environmental conditions of the study area. Therefore, the 2022 application should be interpreted as an assessment of the model’s applicability under data-scarce conditions, rather than as an independent validation of current soil salinity. Overall, the findings highlight the value of legacy soil datasets for soil salinity modelling while demonstrating that, for this study area, satellite-derived salinity indices and NDVI alone are insufficient to reliably characterize soil salinity.</jats:p>
title: Predicting soil salinity using legacy soil data and sentinel-2 imagery: a machine learning approach

items.abstract: <jats:p>As a cornerstone of automated surgical analysis, surgical phase recognition plays a pivotal role in providing dynamic decision support for surgical robotics. However, complex intraoperative factors—such as illumination variations, instrument occlusion, and image noise—hinder existing methodologies from accurately capturing and integrating spatial-temporal representations. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an attention-driven spatial-temporal aggregation network for precise and automated surgical phase recognition. Specifically, a domain-enhanced surgical foundation model, LemonFM, is leveraged as a spatial feature encoding backbone to preserve high-fidelity visual context. Subsequently, a novel parallel temporal encoder integrating Transformer units with a dilated residual unit, BiGRU, and xLSTM is designed to comprehensively capture both short-term temporal fluctuations and long-range workflow dynamics. Furthermore, an attention-based fusion unit is developed to deeply aggregate static spatial information and dynamic temporal context through cross-attention, significantly enhancing feature discrimination at complex phase transitions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance on benchmark datasets, reaching 90.7% accuracy, 84.9% precision, and 87.0% recall on M2CAI16, as well as 92.7% accuracy, 83.6% precision, and 88.8% recall on Cholec80, consistently outperforming current state-of-the-art approaches and offering a powerful technical framework for intelligent computer-assisted surgery.</jats:p>
title: An Attention-Driven Spatial-Temporal Aggregation Network for Surgical Phase Recognition

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Fused filament fabrication (FFF) has gained substantial attention in additive manufacturing for making lightweight functional structural components. However, the mechanical performance of FFF-fabricated parts is heavily impacted by several interdependent processing parameters, making accurate prediction challenging. This study aims to establish a precise machine learning-based framework to forecast the tensile characteristics of polyamide–carbon fiber reinforced polymer composites made using the FFF technique.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A thorough experimental data set was developed by systematically adjusting key FFF processing parameters, including nozzle temperature, layer height, infill density, printing speed and infill pattern. Machine learning models, particularly random forest, Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) and Light gradient boosting machine (GBM), were created to predict tensile strength, Young’s modulus and elongation at break. Model performance was evaluated using the coefficient of determination (R2), and feature importance analysis was conducted to determine the most relevant process parameters.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among the examined models, XGBoost had the highest predictive accuracy, reaching R2 values of 0.998 for the training data set and 0.956 for the test data set. LightGBM displayed greater generalization ability for all three mechanical properties. The five-fold cross validation showed mean R2 values of 0.921 for ultimate tensile strength, 0.871 for Young’s modulus and 0.889 for elongation demonstrating the robustness of the models. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis indicated layer height as the most important parameter, followed by nozzle temperature and infill density.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This research includes various steps such as mechanical property prediction based on data, automatic hyperparameters optimization using Optuna, comparison of various machine learning models, multi-objective optimization by means of NSGA-III and explanation of the artificial intelligence model by SHAP. The suggested method markedly diminishes experimental workload and material wastage, offering a rapid and efficient instrument for optimizing processes and predicting mechanical properties in additive manufacturing.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Machine learning based prediction of tensile strength properties of fused filament fabricated PA-CFRP composites

items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Chronic diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) pose a severe clinical hurdle, largely because of the resilience of polymicrobial biofilms. When
                    <jats:italic>Staphylococcus aureus</jats:italic>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>Pseudomonas aeruginosa</jats:italic>
                    occupy the same wound environment, they can form a drug-tolerant biofilm in which context-dependent cooperation, regulated in part by species-specific quorum sensing (QS) systems, contributes to persistence. Single-target treatments do not address the regulatory programmes of both organisms. This perspective proposes, but does not implement a computational strategy that combines machine learning, multi-task virtual screening, and a staged experimental cascade to prioritize dual-acting QS inhibitors. We hypothesize that the Gram-negative LasR receptor and the Gram-positive AgrA regulator, although structurally unrelated, share enough pharmacophore-level ligandability for a single small molecule to inhibit both. Such dual inhibition of two species-specific QS pathways is distinct from direct disruption of interspecies signaling, which would require separate evidence. We distinguish established evidence from hypothesis and proposed methodology, set out a convergence test and falsifiable go/no-go criteria, and discuss data harmonization, model validation and wound-specific constraints. If the hypothesis holds, such a compound could act as an antivirulence adjuvant that may enhance the activity of conventional antibiotics under selected conditions and support wound healing.
                  </jats:p>
title: A proposed multi-task machine learning strategy for dual-target quorum sensing inhibitor discovery in diabetic foot ulcer biofilms

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Pervious concrete (PC) serves as a highly porous pavement material enabling water infiltration, stormwater runoff reduction, and groundwater recharge. PC properties are often governed by factors such as aggregate shape, size, and pore characteristics, cement content, water–cement ratio, and additives. Although machine learning (ML) has transformed the construction industry by predicting conventional concrete properties, studies on PC with additives remain limited. Thus, the major objective of this study was to assess the effectiveness of ML models and algorithms in predicting the target properties of PC mixtures, including compressive strength (CS), porosity, and permeability, based on random forest (RF), gradient boosting (GB), and artificial neural network (ANN) using a master database of 350 data points covering 78 mixtures. An independent 36-point external validation set was used to assess model generalizability. The input parameters used for developing the models included water-to-cement ratio, aggregate-to-cement (a/c) ratio, density, and additives such as silica fume and crumb rubber. Performance metrics indicated that RF and GB outperformed ANN during CS prediction, with test coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.79 and 0.80, and root mean square error of 2.04 and 1.97 MPa, respectively. Further, mixture-level out-of-fold R2 of 0.45 (RF) and 0.44 (GB) represented the unbiased estimates. All three models predicted porosity and permeability with good to excellent accuracy (R2 = 0.83–0.98). Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations-based feature importance analysis revealed that density dominated CS prediction, and the a/c ratio governed porosity and permeability, thereby corroborating the distinct physical mechanisms controlling the mechanical and hydraulic performance of PC. All three ML models predicted the target PC properties with very good to excellent accuracy; however, the RF model showed the narrowest expected difference range (d3s) for predicted PC properties. It is envisioned that the proposed algorithms in this study can be readily applied in practice by entering component quantities in the same format as the training dataset. Overall, this research study contributed to comprehending the PC properties better and will serve as the foundation for a computational and statistical framework in the future to facilitate a paradigm shift toward developing environmentally sustainable and resilient roadway infrastructure materials/systems.</jats:p>
title: Assessing the Effectiveness of Machine Learning Models in Predicting the Target Properties of Modified Pervious Concrete Mixtures

items.abstract: <jats:p>INTRODUCTION: Inter-individual variation of glucose dynamics confounds generic "one-size-fits-all" forecasting models of continuous glucose monitoring data. We developed a phenotype-stratified evaluation framework to characterize a model's performance and its complementarity for short-term glucose prediction across different patient profiles. METHODS: To analyze the data from CGMs of 44 adults. Principal Component Analysis and Fuzzy C-means clustering methods were applied and resulted in 3 latent glycemic phenotypes. Inside each cluster, we built a 4-state Gaussian hidden Markov model and an autoregressive eXtreme Gradient Boosting model. Models were validated on held-out data at 15, 30, 60, and 120 min horizon by Mean Absolute Error, Root Mean Square Error, and Mean Absolute Relative Difference. RESULTS: Three clinically meaningful glycemic phenotypes were identified from the PCA and Fuzzy C-Means. XGBoost, for the most part, had the lower average error metrics compared to the HMM. However, a large quantity of complementarity was seen with neither model being always the winner with phenotype and horizon-dependent preferences for HMM, XGBoost, or any similar performances. The HMM offers strong and understandable insights into hidden glycemic states and their transitions, enhancing the predictive capabilities of XGBoost. CONCLUSIONS: Our framework demonstrates great heterogeneity in the performance of CGM forecasting. The presence of a meaningful complementarity between HMM and XGBoost suggests that adaptive and phenotypeinformed model selection methods would prove to be more effective than any of the individual global models and can provide a practical template for personalized management for diabetes.</jats:p>
title: Integrated Glycemic Phenotypes for Glucose Prediction: A Comparative Study Using Hidden Markov Models and Machine Learning

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines contextual challenges in integrating AI and ML (Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning) into telecommunications engineering education in Zimbabwean state universities. Although there is global attention on AI/ML for improving engineering practices, graduates from Zimbabwe lack competencies in these areas because curricula are misaligned with infrastructure constraints. A mixed-methods multi-site study of 190 students, 20 faculty members and 35 industry experts was undertaken to understand experiences and perceptions of integration of AI/ML. Students were interested in AI/ML (84.2%), but only 53.2% had exposure to the concepts in formal curriculum (interest vs delivery gap); resources (69.5%), infrastructure (48.4%) and syllabi (33.7%) were challenges identified. A statistically significant association was found between study level and AI/ML awareness (χ² = 42.187, df = 4, p < .001, Cramér's V = .333) after collapsing sparse categories to satisfy Cochran's assumption. A context-sensitive framework for AI/ML integration is proposed, comprising four interconnected components: inputs, enablers, integration touch-points, and reform stages. Context-sensitive curriculum reforms and industry partnerships are required to improve educational outcomes and better prepare graduates for the changing technological landscape. This work helps us understand how to implement AI/ML in resource-poor schools and provides practical guidance for those who design curriculum and implement it.</jats:p>
title: A Study on Integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) into Telecommunications Engineering Education to Improve Learning Outcomes for Zimbabwe State Universities

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Due to the pollution and high carbon footprint associated with the use of fossil fuels, alternative renewable energy sources continue to be a challenge for scientific studies. We herein present our novel approach that utilizes food waste to obtain environmentally friendly energy sources. We first turned bread waste, which makes up a high amount of food waste globally, into glucose‐containing culture medium for algal growth by yeast hydrolysis. Then, we examined the growth of
                    <jats:italic>Chlorella vulgaris</jats:italic>
                    under various environmental conditions in this modified culture medium. Our results confirmed that
                    <jats:italic>C. vulgaris</jats:italic>
                    growth increased at least fivefold in bread waste culture medium and higher amounts of algae biomass were obtained. Moreover, our bread waste‐based medium supported the production of higher amounts of lipid, which meet the biodiesel quality requirements in terms of saturated to unsaturated lipid ratio, saponification value, iodine value, and cetane number. Dry weight as high as 1.8 g L
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    and lipid yield of 500 mg L
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    could be achieved with the bread waste‐based modified medium. Moreover, the omega‐3 (ω‐3) yield obtained using modified culture medium was also increased and it can be regarded as a value‐added side product that promotes profit margin. We have also developed a MATLAB‐based graphical user interface for the prediction dry weight, lipid yield, and ω‐3 percentage based on various microalgae production conditions. According to the study's findings, the fivefold increase in biomass production and the achievement of biodiesel profiles complying with European standards demonstrate a high potential for using microalgae in biotechnological applications, producing sustainable energy, and turning waste into products with added value.
                  </jats:p>
title: Optimization of microalgae production from bread waste using Box–Behnken design and machine learning algorithms

items.abstract: <jats:p>Optimizing the operating modes of hydrotreating units is difficult because the parameters are numerous and interdependent, and product-quality indicators are often available only as fuzzy expert assessments. This study integrates fuzzy modeling, a heuristic decision-making method, and machine learning into a unified framework for controlling a hydrotreating unit. A system of models was developed for the reactor, three columns, and the furnace, combining nonlinear regression for measurable parameters, fuzzy regression for quality indicators, and a furnace heat balance. The reactor control problem with fuzzy quality constraints was solved by the AorRA + PO heuristic (absolute or relative allowance with Pareto optimality). In parallel, eight regression algorithms were compared on a synthetic dataset whose quality model was built independently from reaction kinetics; the best gradient-boosting models (R2 = 0.98–0.99) served as a process surrogate for optimization. The fuzzy approach raised the product volume to 77.5 m3/h (2.0% above the deterministic method); the machine-learning approach reached 79.6 m3/h (+2.7%) with the quality constraints met (Score = 0.90). Although the generator contained no information about the heuristic solution, the machine-learning optimum reproduced its temperature, confirming the agreement of the two methods. Because the models were trained on synthetic data, the recommended mode requires experimental verification.</jats:p>
title: Optimization of Hydrotreating Unit Operating Mode Control Based on Machine Learning Models and a Heuristic Method

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In recent years, the growing frequency and severity of natural disasters have increased the need for effective tools to manage catastrophe risk. Catastrophe (CAT) bonds allow the transfer of part of this risk to investors, offering an alternative to traditional reinsurance. This paper examines the role of climate variability in CAT bond pricing and evaluates the predictive performance of various machine learning models in forecasting CAT bond coupons. We combine features typically used in the literature with a new set of climate indicators, including Oceanic Niño Index, Arctic Oscillation, North Atlantic Oscillation, Outgoing Longwave Radiation, Pacific–North American pattern, Pacific Decadal Oscillation, Southern Oscillation Index, and sea surface temperatures. We compare the performance of linear regression with several machine learning algorithms, such as random forest, gradient boosting, extremely randomized trees, and extreme gradient boosting. Our results show that including climate-related variables improves predictive accuracy across all models, with extremely randomized trees achieving the lowest root mean squared error (RMSE). These findings suggest that large-scale climate variability has a measurable influence on CAT bond pricing and that machine learning methods can effectively capture these complex relationships.</jats:p>
title: Machine learning models for predicting catastrophe bond coupons using climate data

items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Accurate prediction of the martensite start temperature (
                    <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>s</jats:sub>
                    ) is critical for the design and industrial processing of advanced steels. This article provides a comprehensive state‐of‐the‐art review of
                    <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>s</jats:sub>
                    prediction methods spanning eight decades (1940–2025), organized into four methodological eras: empirical linear regression, thermodynamic CALPHAD‐based models, pure machine learning approaches, and hybrid physics‐informed ML. All methods are evaluated within a four‐dimensional framework encompassing accuracy, accessibility, uncertainty quantification (UQ), and sustainability. Hybrid ML–physics models achieve root‐mean‐square errors (RMSE) of 12.15–14 K with
                    <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    up to 0.95 on novel compositions, representing a substantial improvement over earlier empirical equations while reducing CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    emissions by four to five orders of magnitude relative to full CALPHAD workflows. Standardized UQ evaluation protocols and a practitioner decision framework mapping use‐case scenarios to recommended methods are proposed. Emerging roles of large language models and generative AI (GenAI) in
                    <jats:italic>M</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sub>s</jats:sub>
                    research, open reproducibility challenges, and ethical governance considerations are also addressed.

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry is widely used for distributed acoustic sensing, yet effective event recognition in multi-source interference environments remains a significant challenge. To address these issues, this paper proposes a lightweight and efficient separation framework based on the time–frequency interleaved gain extraction and reconstruction (TIGER) architecture. A uniform band-split strategy replaces the speech-oriented frequency allocation, while multi-scale processing and attention model the temporal and spectral structure of the mixtures. Experiments cover six event classes, two-source and three-source synthetic mixtures, and real simultaneous two-source recordings. Comparisons include ConvTasNet Base and Tiny, dual-path recurrent neural network, SuDoRM-RF, TF-GridNet, and TIGER with the adapted original band split. Uniform-band TIGER achieves per-source classification accuracies of 97.17 ± 0.16% and 94.74 ± 0.01% with 0.822 M and 0.779 M parameters in the two-source and three-source tasks, respectively. Relative to the original-band variant, it improves accuracy by 2.29 and 1.79 percentage points and scale-invariant source-to-distortion ratio by 0.509 and 0.430 dB. In the three-source task, TIGER uses 9.5% of the parameters of TF-GridNet, with an accuracy difference of 0.87 percentage points. On 21 real two-source windows, it achieves an 87.30 ± 2.75% both-events-correct rate despite measurable differences between real and synthetic input features. Repeated training and paired test-mixture analysis support the performance comparisons. On an RTX 4090, the three-source separator processes a 0.5 s input in 73.69 ms, giving a real-time factor of 0.147. The results establish uniform-band adaptation as an effective approach to compact separation-based multi-event perception.</jats:p>
title: Lightweight separation-based multi-event perception for distributed acoustic sensing

items.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid, non-destructive assessment of fruit quality is increasingly important for optimizing grading and sorting operations, reducing postharvest losses, and enhancing supply-chain efficiency. Among stone fruits, plum (Prunus domestica L.) represents an economically important crop worldwide. Accurate assessment of its commercial and nutritional quality is essential for determining fruit suitability for different market destinations and end uses. This study investigated the potential of portable Vis/NIR hyperspectral imaging (400–1000 nm) combined with artificial neural networks (ANNs) for a non-destructive prediction of total soluble solids (TSS), titratable acidity (TA), and the sugar to acid ratio (TSS/TA), a parameter widely associated with consumer sensory acceptability. Six plum cultivars differing in fruit size and skin color were analyzed over two consecutive growing seasons (2023 and 2024). Significant variability was observed among cultivars in both biometric and physicochemical traits. The developed ANN models demonstrated high predictive performance for all investigated quality parameters. For TSS, the coefficients of determination (R2) were 0.975, 0.950, and 0.984 for the training, test, and validation datasets, respectively. Similarly, TA prediction yielded R2 values of 0.984, 0.977, and 0.958, while the corresponding values for TSS/TA were 0.919, 0.915, and 0.928. External validation using an independent dataset of fruits harvested in 2025 further supported the predictive reliability and temporal robustness of the models, with R2 values exceeding 0.91 for all three quality traits. Sensitivity analysis identified the most informative spectral regions within the visible region (approximately 400–450 and 650–670 nm) and near-infrared ranges (760 and 1000 nm), suggesting that model predictions were influenced by spectral features associated with fruit pigmentation, tissue structure, water status, and chemical composition. Overall, these findings highlight the potential of integrating portable hyperspectral imaging with artificial neural networks as a reliable and non-destructive approach for the prediction of key plum quality attributes.</jats:p>
title: Rapid and Non-Destructive Assessment of Quality in Plums by Vis/NIR Hyperspectral Imaging and Machine Learning

items.abstract: <jats:p>We tested whether large language models (LLMs) can tune the settings (hyperparameters) of machine-learning fraud detectors. In a pre-registered study on three public fraud benchmarks, Claude Opus 5.5 proposed settings for XGBoost and LightGBM and was compared with random search and a Bayesian optimiser (TPE); every model was tested on a later period than it was tuned on, with 10 repeats per condition. After 10 trials, the LLM’s median PR-AUC was within the pre-registered margin of 0.005 of TPE’s after 40 trials on two benchmarks, with non-inferiority shown in three of these four comparisons; on the third benchmark it was 0.008–0.011 lower. In a post hoc comparison, a smaller model, Claude Haiku 5.5, was non-inferior to Opus at about 3% of the fees. Naming the dataset met the pre-registered rule for an advantage, but the gains were negligible (at most 0.003). The LLM’s proposals followed altered trial scores in 79% of cases, which shows sensitivity to the evidence but does not exclude memorised knowledge. With only 28 frauds in the tuning data, no reliable positive relation between tuning scores and later performance was detected. Contrary to common advice, tuning on the most recent data did not select better models than tuning on a random sample; a post hoc controlled refit indicated that both the number of trees chosen by early stopping and the selected settings contributed to this gap. The evidence is limited to three benchmarks and two gradient-boosting libraries.</jats:p>
title: Can Large Language Models Tune Fraud Detection Models? Evidence from Three Public Fraud Datasets

items.abstract: <jats:p>Pairs trading relies critically on selecting pairs with stable and exploitable relationships. Traditional approaches typically use a single criterion, such as distance, correlation, or cointegration, potentially overlooking the multidimensional characteristics of candidate pairs. This study proposes a supervised machine learning framework combined with traditional pair-selection methods to rank cryptocurrency pairs according to their expected trading performance. Four statistical features, namely, the ADF p-value, Hurst exponent, half-life, and spread volatility, are used as inputs to the machine learning models. In addition to standalone traditional and machine learning rankings, an equal-weight hybrid approach is introduced by assigning 50% weight to each ranking component. The dataset is divided chronologically into three periods: 2022–2023 for model training, 2024 for validation and model selection, and 2025 for final out-of-sample testing. The proposed framework is evaluated using Top-1, Top-5, Top-10, Top-20 and Top-40 portfolios based on total return, volatility, Sharpe ratio, Sortino ratio, maximum drawdown, number of trades, and profit factor. The results show that performance depends strongly on portfolio size. The correlation-based hybrid approach achieves the highest Sharpe ratio for Top-1, Top-5, Top-10, and Top-40 portfolios, while the standalone machine learning model performs best for Top-20. Feature importance results indicate that the four input variables contribute relatively similar shares to the model, with spread volatility having the highest relative importance. Robustness analyses further show that the selected methods outperform random pair selection across all portfolio sizes, with statistically significant differences in four of the five cases. The results also remain broadly comparable when an alternative target definition based on median Sharpe ratios is used. Overall, the findings demonstrate that supervised learning provides a flexible framework for integrating heterogeneous pair characteristics and improving cryptocurrency pair selection.</jats:p>
title: Optimizing Risk–Return in Pairs Trading via Hybrid Econometric–Machine Learning Framework

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>HIV testing is a central entry point to prevention and care, yet uptake remains uneven across population groups. Although many demographic and behavioral correlates are known, the incremental predictive contribution of service-access opportunities and the geographic transportability of prediction models remain unclear.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We analyzed 2024 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System data from 245,683 adults aged 18–64 years with known lifetime HIV testing status. Twenty-nine predictors were organized using Andersen’s Behavioral Model into predisposing, enabling/service-access, and need/health-behavior domains. Survey-weighted penalized logistic regression, extreme gradient boosting, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine models were evaluated in a held-out test set using discrimination, calibration, and state-stratified bootstrap confidence intervals. We compared models with sequentially added domains and with all domain combinations, validated the model in held-out states, explained predictions with Shapley additive explanations, assessed performance by subgroup and without protected attributes, and examined a hypothetical capacity-constrained outreach scenario.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Weighted lifetime HIV testing prevalence was 45.6%. Extreme gradient boosting achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.740 (95% confidence interval 0.730–0.749), area under the precision-recall curve of 0.697, Brier score of 0.205, and calibration slope of 0.978. Enabling/service-access factors increased AUROC from 0.700 to 0.715 beyond predisposing factors (difference 0.015, 95% confidence interval 0.011–0.020); need/health-behavior factors increased it further to 0.740. Added last to predisposing and need/health-behavior factors, enabling/service-access factors increased AUROC by 0.006 (95% confidence interval 0.003–0.009). Under a hypothetical outreach capacity of 20% of adults, the model would select an estimated 16,433 never-tested adults per 100,000 adults, versus 10,840 under random selection; adding enabling/service-access factors to predisposing factors increased this number by 316 (95% confidence interval 48–589). Among enabling/service-access factors, routine checkup recency contributed most to model predictions. In state held-out cross-validation, the mean AUROC was 0.736.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Service-access characteristics add modest incremental predictive information beyond demographic composition and, to a smaller degree, beyond need and health-behavior factors. The model may inform health system and community outreach planning, but its moderate discrimination does not justify its use for individual clinical decisions or as a service-restriction rule.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Service-access factors add predictive information for lifetime HIV testing among United States adults: a survey-weighted explainable machine-learning study

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Osteopenia and osteoporosis are common in routine health-examination populations, but cross-sectional indices must not be interpreted as predictors of incident fractures.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To compare routinely derived anthropometric, metabolic and inflammatory indices in relation to prevalent lower bone mass and to explore internal classification performance.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this cross-sectional study, we analyzed 848 adults attending health examinations in 2024–2025. Bone mineral density was assessed by central dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry at the lumbar spine, femoral neck, and total hip. Bone status was classified using the lowest recorded T-score: normal (≥−1.0), osteopenia (−2.5 &lt; T-score &lt; −1.0), or osteoporosis (≤−2.5). Three borderline classifications were retained as recorded. Because Z-scores were unavailable, diagnostic terminology for premenopausal women and men younger than 50 years requires caution. We examined adjusted associations, quartiles, restricted cubic splines, sensitivity analyses, internal model performance, and exploratory clusters.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Of 848 participants, 397 (46.8%) had normal bone mass, 351 (41.4%) osteopenia, and 100 (11.8%) osteoporosis. The fully adjusted odds ratios (95% CIs) per 1 SD were 1.61 (1.25–2.06) for WWI, 1.59 (1.23–2.05) for conicity index, 1.34 (1.01–1.79) for TyG–WHtR, 1.41 (1.12–1.77) for SII, and 0.71 (0.53–0.96) for BMI. After false-discovery-rate correction across 25 indices, TyG–WHtR was no longer statistically significant (q=0.119). In the held-out test sample, the AUROC was 0.948 (95% bootstrap CI 0.92–0.97) for the demographic model and 0.947 (0.92–0.97) for the novel-index model (paired difference −0.001, 95% CI −0.02 to 0.01).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Central adiposity and inflammatory indices were associated with existing lower bone mass, but the new-index model did not improve discrimination over basic demographic characteristics. Prospective and external studies are needed before these measures can inform clinical decisions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: Central adiposity, insulin resistance, and systemic inflammation in osteopenia and osteoporosis: a hospital-based study using explainable machine learning

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>γδ T cells are unconventional T cells harboring features of innate and adaptive response. Indeed, they express both TCR receptors, interacting with their target in a mostly MHC independent manner, and NK receptors, conferring them cytotoxic characteristics. Actually, clinical scale in-vitro expanded γδ T cells (DOT cell procedure) are currently in clinical trial in Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML). This sub-population is specifically enriched in tissues and their number in tumors associates with better survival in different solid cancers. These characteristics make them of great interest to develop therapeutic agents in tumors with low mutational burden or low HLA-I expression, such as glioblastomas (GBM). GBM are the most frequent and aggressive primary brain malignancies, with very limited therapeutic options and a dismal prognosis. So far, immunotherapies evaluated in clinical trials have failed to provide significant clinical benefit for GBM patients, notably due to the high genetic heterogeneity and immunosuppressive environment of the tumor. Here, we aimed at developing a new cell therapy strategy in GBM, using in-vitro expanded γδ T cells.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Material and Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Amplified γδ Tcells (DOTs) were produced based on Almeida et al., 2016 protocol. Initially, cytotoxic assays were used to assess their capacity in vitro against different GBM cell lines and patient-derived glioblastoma stem cells (GSCs). DOT cells were also assessed in-vivo by adoptive transfer in patient-derived xenograft mouse models, evaluating different administration modes : intravenously and intratumorally, in immunodeficient Rag γ 2C-/- mice with intraperitoneal injections of interleukin 15 (IL-15) or in NOG mice expressing human IL-15.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In vitro models showed 𝛾;𝛿; T cells capacity to efficiently kill multiple GBM cell lines, including primary-derived GSCs. Their cytotoxic activity was increased by adding IL-15 in the cell culture medium. We then sought to develop a murine model of cell therapy to assess 𝛾;𝛿; T cells efficiency in vivo. Although 𝛾;𝛿; T cells did not reach the brain after multiple intravenous injections, due to the blood-brain-barrier, intra-tumoral injections showed encouraging results with a delay in the tumor growth observed after some injections. These results were stronger in the NOG-IL15 model. Further characterization of donor variability is ongoing in these models.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These data provide in vitro and show encouraging in vivo proof of concept for off-the-shelf use of γδ T cells to target GBM.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: P08.23.A Gamma delta T cell therapy against glioblastoma

items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents a unified Perturb and Observe (P&O) Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) strategy for a small-scale hybrid renewable energy system integrating a vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT) and a photovoltaic (PV) source through a single buck converter. Unlike conventional approaches employing separate MPPT controllers for individual renewable energy sources, the proposed Unified P&O MPPT strategy uses the total harvested power of the PV–VAWT system as the optimization variable and generates a single duty-ratio command for the buck converter. The proposed control scheme is developed and evaluated using MATLAB/Simulink and experimentally validated using a dSPACE-based control and measurement platform. Simulation results demonstrate the generation of the individual PV and wind power responses, the combined total harvested power, and the corresponding duty-ratio control for 12V battery charging. Experimental results further verify the practical operation of the proposed controller, including the generation of the PWM control signal, buck-converter operation, and battery charging. In addition, source-combination tests demonstrate successful transitions from PV-only to hybrid PV–VAWT operation and from VAWT-only to hybrid VAWT–PV operation while maintaining continuous power-conversion operation. The results demonstrate that the proposed Unified P&O MPPT strategy provides a simple and practical control approach for coordinated power extraction from small-scale PV and VAWT sources using a single power-conversion stage.</jats:p>
title: A Unified P&O MPPT Strategy for a Single Buck Converter in Small-Scale VAWT–PV Hybrid Energy Systems

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study proposes a Dual-Interleaved Boost Converter (DIBC) as an improvement over the conventional In-terleaved Boost Converter (IBC) to enhance voltage conversion capability and performance characteristics. The DIBC is built using a two-level interleaved boost converter configuration arranged in a cascade. The per-formance of both topologies is evaluated using PSIM simulation with an input voltage of 18 V and a switching frequency of 20 kHz. The IBC is operated at a 50% duty cycle, while the DIBC uses a 70% duty cycle. The simu-lation results show that the IBC produces a steady-state output voltage of 36.00 V, while the DIBC reaches 199.97 V. Ripple analysis shows that the DIBC has an absolute output voltage of 1.030 V and a ripple current of 0.069 A, higher than the IBC's 0.241 V and 0.005 A, respectively. However, after normalizing to their respec-tive output values, the DIBC produces a ripple voltage of 0.517% and a ripple current of 0.51%, compared to 0.669% and 0.69% for the IBC. In terms of power, the IBC produces an input power of 44.00 W and an output power of 37.08 W with an efficiency of 84.27%, while the DIBC produces an input power of 2798.10 W and an output power of 2640.66 W with an efficiency of 94.37%. Transient response analysis shows that the DIBC reaches steady state in approximately 0.87 s, faster than the IBC which requires approximately 1.84 s under the test conditions used. These results indicate that the DIBC has high step-up voltage conversion capability, good normalized ripple characteristics, higher simulation efficiency, and faster steady-state response under the evaluated operating conditions. Further research is needed through non-ideal component modeling, varying operating conditions, and experimental validation to more comprehensively confirm the performance of the DIBC.</jats:p>
title: A Novel Dual Interleaved Boost Converter Topology for Improved Efficiency and Dynamic Response

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Researchers rarely work alone: they work with colleagues within and between organizations on all organizational levels. They collaborate on a variety of research results beyond traditional publications. However, collaboration indicators in research assessment usually rely on a single source, focus on top-level institutions, and may focus on journal articles only. This limits what can be seen about collaborations within organizations, and for results such as data sets and software. This article introduces a multi-source, multi-level, graph-based approach to collaboration indicators using Ricgraph (Research in context graph). Publications, data sets, software, persons, and organizational information from multiple systems are integrated into a single graph. Collaborations are defined as shared research results connecting organizations via persons. They are quantified on top-level organization, as well as on faculty and departmental level, providing a concrete operationalization of multi-source, multi-level collaboration indicators for science-of-science research. Combining multiple sources substantially increases the observed coverage of collaborations, especially for data set and software collaborations (&gt;400% for sources in this article, compared to a single source). Multi-level collaborations overviews reveal patterns that are invisible at the top-level alone. These results illustrate how multi-source, multi-level, graph-based collaboration indicators can complement citation-based metrics in responsible research assessment and institutional evaluation.</jats:p>
title: Multi-source, multi-level, graph-based institutional collaboration indicators for research assessment with Ricgraph

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates spatial segregation in "swarm" sounds, a class of auditory textures arising from multiples of rhythmic sound elements modeled on collective swarm dynamics in nature. Such sounds provide a controlled framework, inspired by naturally occurring textures, for exploring how rhythmic signals can be detected within dense auditory textures. Using ensembles of metronomes to approximate such swarms, we examined how density and spatial separation affect listeners' ability to detect and synchronize with an embedded target rhythm. Thirteen participants tapped along with a target metronome presented at varying azimuthal angles (0° to 65°) relative to a swarm masker directly ahead, with density varied across ten levels (200 to 920 sources). Detection probability increased with angular separation and decreased with swarm density, with a significant detection interaction suggesting that denser textures expand the spatial masking region. At low densities, reliable detection occurred at approximately 21°, while higher densities required separations of 29° or greater. Synchronization accuracy, measured via normalized inter-tap intervals, was reduced near the detection threshold, and reaction times increased under challenging spatial conditions. In general, the findings indicate that spatial position and source density jointly shape the extent to which rhythmic targets can be detected by sensorimotor synchronization.</jats:p>
title: Detecting Rhythmic Signals in "Swarm" Auditory Textures: Effects of Source Position, Density, and Synchronization Ability

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The assessment of physical education curriculum quality has traditionally relied on limited data sources and static evaluation methods, which often fail to capture the dynamic and multifaceted nature of educational environments. This paper introduces a novel methodology that leverages multi source teaching data to enhance intelligent assessment and personalized feedback mechanisms. The approach is organized into three core components: Preliminaries, the Adaptive Multi Source Integration Model (AMSIM), and the Adaptive Feedback Mechanism (AFM). The Preliminaries section establishes a mathematical framework for the integration of diverse data sources, encompassing student performance metrics, instructor evaluations, and environmental factors. The AMSIM utilizes a multi layered neural network to synthesize these data streams, offering comprehensive insights into curriculum quality. The AFM uses these insights to provide personalized feedback, dynamically adapting to individual student needs and forecasting future performance. This methodology marks a significant advancement in educational assessment, promoting a more engaging and effective learning environment through data driven insights and personalized feedback.</jats:p>
title: Intelligent assessment and personalized feedback mechanism for physical education curriculum quality driven by multi source teaching data

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The Burst Alert Telescope (BAT) on board the Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory is capable of localizing gamma-ray transients with arcminute precision, enabling rapid multiwavelength follow-up. However, onboard triggering is disabled during spacecraft slews, preventing the autonomous detection and localization of transients occurring during these intervals. We present here
                    <jats:monospace>BAT-GLIMPSE</jats:monospace>
                    , a fully autonomous, open-source pipeline for the low-latency localization of transient gamma-ray sources in Swift-BAT data. Making use of the
                    <jats:monospace>BatAnalysis</jats:monospace>
                    package, the pipeline combines coded-mask imaging and mosaic techniques, automatically selecting the appropriate analysis according to the spacecraft attitude and enabling localization searches during both pointing observations and spacecraft slews. We validate the performance of
                    <jats:monospace>BAT-GLIMPSE</jats:monospace>
                    on a sample of 66 gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) reported in GUANO circulars. The pipeline successfully recovers arcminute positions for 43 events, consistent with published localizations, with typical offsets of ≲5′. Approximately 88% of the GRBs occurring during spacecraft slews are recovered through imaging or mosaic analyses. During the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run, the role of
                    <jats:monospace>BAT-GLIMPSE</jats:monospace>
                    was crucial in the search for gamma-ray counterparts of gravitational waves, particularly in response to premerger alerts which triggered the slew of the Swift spacecraft with extremely low latency. Operating synergistically with
                    <jats:monospace>NITRATES</jats:monospace>
                    ,
                    <jats:monospace>BAT-GLIMPSE</jats:monospace>
                    fills the critical gap left by slew intervals and, together, the two pipelines are estimated to double the onboard arcminute-localization rate of Swift-BAT, unlocking the full potential of the Swift mission for time-domain and multimessenger astrophysics.
                  </jats:p>
title:
Swift Gives a New
                    <tt>BAT-GLIMPSE</tt>
                    : Gamma-Ray Localization Using Imaging and Mosaic Techniques for Pointing and Slew Epochs

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>As AI systems become increasingly embedded in medicine, policing, warfare, and other high-stakes domains, their harmful outputs raise a pressing question: who, if anyone, is morally responsible? A common worry is that AI can generate responsibility gaps: cases in which morally significant harms occur, human agents acted suboptimally, and yet no individual seems to satisfy the conditions for accountability. Such gaps are troubling because they threaten practices of blame, compensation, deterrence, and moral repair. But when and why do responsibility gaps arise? Existing discussions often locate the source of the gap in either the opacity of AI systems or the involvement of many human contributors. This paper argues that both diagnoses miss the mark. The real source of AI responsibility gaps, we argue, is overdetermination. In many AI contexts, harmful outcomes may occur regardless of what any particular individual does, because other agents, firms, institutions, or systems would have produced materially similar outcomes. This structure undermines the control condition on moral responsibility. The diagnosis matters for our evaluations of remedies: transparency-based solutions target the wrong sort of problem, and individual gatekeeper models may simply reproduce the same overdetermination structure at a higher level. Collective-level solutions, by contrast, are at least structurally suited to closing the gap.</jats:p>
title: AI and Overdetermination: The Real Source of Responsibility Gaps

items.abstract: <jats:p>Rainfall and Mekong River flow along the riverfront of upper Northeast Thailand drive agriculture and flood risk. We present NAGA-RF, a framework that links three established statistical components through one quality-controlled dataset: a trend-adjusted mixed-Gamma model for monthly rainfall (NAGA-R), a seasonal autoregressive model for monthly discharge at Nakhon Phanom (NAGA-Q), and a block-bootstrap procedure for conditional statistical extrapolation (NAGA-P). Daily records from four Thai Meteorological Department stations (1995–2025) were gap-filled with 3-hourly data, agreeing within 0.1 mm on 99.7% of withheld days. Minimum temperature rose by 0.42–0.46 °C per decade at all three long-record stations, whereas no rainfall trend remained significant after false discovery rate control. Dry-season discharge was 49% higher after 2013 (95% interval 33–67%); the wet-season decline (−25%) depended on the 2019–2023 low-flow years. In leakage-free rolling-origin forecasts for 2010–2025, NAGA-R did not differ from climatology in skill (continuous ranked probability skill score −0.001; 95% interval −0.014 to 0.011) but was well calibrated (80% interval coverage 79.7%). NAGA-Q reached a Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.80 against 0.48 for persistence, while local rainfall added no significant out-of-sample skill. If trends persist, minimum temperature would be 0.9, 1.1, and 2.0 °C above the 1995–2024 normal by 2030, 2035, and 2055, respectively.</jats:p>
title: NAGA-RF: A Nonstationary Adaptive Gamma–Autoregressive Framework for Rainfall and Mekong Discharge Forecasting Along the Upper Northeast Thailand Riverfront

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We estimate the impact of cultural diversity on urban wage and rent premiums by means of hedonic regressions in a spatial equilibrium setting. Our estimates are based on a very large data set from Aotearoa New Zealand: complete unit record census data from 1981 until 2018 on individuals and dwellings in 110 urban areas. Various measures of cultural diversity are considered, including those that account for dissimilarity between groups. Controlling for observed and unobserved city characteristics, and for the potential endogeneity of diversity, we find that cultural diversity serves as a local positive production amenity and a weakly negative consumption amenity. The results are mostly robust to variation in the selection of samples of urban areas and census years; and to variation in the ways in which diversity can be quantified. We conclude that the presence of people from different cultural backgrounds enhances the profitability of urban firms but, at the same time, local populations exhibit a weak preference for living near others who are culturally like them.</jats:p>
title: Cultural Diversity as a Source of Local Urban Production and Consumption Amenities

<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder whose manifestations can be observed through speech, gait, and clinical assessment measures. Machine learning methods have shown potential for automated PD assessment; however, reported performance can be substantially affected by the validation strategy when multiple observations from the same participant are present.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study presents an explainable multi-source framework for evaluating speech-, gait-, and clinical telemonitoring-based Parkinson’s disease assessment with particular emphasis on subject-independent validation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Three publicly available datasets were analyzed independently because they originate from different cohorts and do not provide a common patient-level population suitable for direct multi-source assessment. The UCI Parkinson’s Speech dataset contains 195 recordings, the Parkinson’s Telemonitoring dataset contains 5,875 observations from 42 subjects, and the PhysioNet Gait in Parkinson’s Disease dataset contains 113 recordings. Speech and gait were evaluated as binary classification tasks, while total UPDRS was evaluated as a regression task. Subject-independent validation was performed using grouped cross-validation based on participant identifiers. Model performance was assessed using multiple classification and regression metrics, and SHAP-based analysis was used to improve model interpretability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Under subject-wise validation, the speech classifier achieved a mean accuracy of 77.26 ± 15.87%, balanced accuracy of 66.54 ± 25.42%, sensitivity of 90.57 ± 10.87%, specificity of 42.50 ± 46.81%, and ROC-AUC of 0.7845 ± 0.2461. The gait classifier achieved an accuracy of 68.26 ± 15.89%, balanced accuracy of 63.26 ± 16.24%, sensitivity of 78.67 ± 21.81%, specificity of 47.86 ± 28.72%, and ROC-AUC of 0.726 ± 0.169. Subject-wise total UPDRS regression achieved an MAE of 9.918 ± 1.545, RMSE of 12.220 ± 1.770, and R
                      <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                      of −0.393 ± 0.399.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Subject-independent validation produced substantially lower performance than record-wise evaluation across all three data sources, highlighting the importance of controlling subject-level dependence in Parkinson’s disease machine learning studies. The speech and gait classifiers showed limited specificity, while the UPDRS regression model did not outperform the training-fold mean baseline. The proposed EMDF framework provides an explainable, subject-aware methodology for independently evaluating heterogeneous data sources without unsupported patient-level fusion across cohorts.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: An explainable multi-source framework for Parkinson’s disease diagnosis and progression prediction using speech, gait, and clinical biomarkers

<jats:p>Paediatric stroke is uncommon, and intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) associated with severe hypertension is particularly rare. Renovascular disease is an important, potentially treatable cause of secondary hypertension in children, but it may not be recognised until target-organ complications occur (deVeber et al., 2017; Lo et al., 2009).
An 11-year-old boy presented with sudden-onset right-sided hemiparesis that progressed rapidly and was followed by transient loss of consciousness. Brain imaging showed a left anterior putaminal haemorrhage measuring 43 × 27 mm, with surrounding oedema and intraventricular extension. His blood pressure was markedly elevated for his age. Intracranial vascular imaging did not identify a vascular malformation. Further evaluation demonstrated reduced left renal arterial flow on Doppler ultrasonography, and CT aortography confirmed complete occlusion of the left renal artery immediately distal to its origin. Echocardiography showed left ventricular hypertrophy. Blood pressure control required sequential use of multiple antihypertensive agents. With conservative neurocritical care and blood pressure control, his neurological status improved, and he was able to walk independently at discharge.
This case underlines the need to investigate secondary causes when a child presents with spontaneous ICH and severe or difficult-to-control hypertension. Timely recognition of renovascular disease and careful management of the hypertensive emergency may help reduce further neurological injury.</jats:p>
title: A Neurological Emergency from a Renal Source: Pediatric Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Case Report

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Bottom-up (BU) inventories and top-down (TD) aerial measurements at midstream natural gas facilities frequently diverge, and this discrepancy remains a central challenge for methane accounting in the sector. Previous approaches typically reconcile this divergence by treating BU and TD data as independent estimates of a single true quantity to be adjusted toward agreement, rather than as evidence that each captures only part of a more complex underlying system. This complexity arises from methane emissions being strongly governed by equipment operational state and therefore instantaneous aerial “snapshots” translate poorly to annual inventories. We argue instead that BU and TD are complementary sources of evidence that should be integrated. We present a source-level Bayesian framework that constructs BU prior distributions for each emission source category and updates them with attributed aerial detections through an empirical data-augmentation procedure. The resulting posterior distributions were propagated through unit-level activity data and source-specific information via Monte Carlo simulation to produce annual estimates. Across 64 compressor stations, measurement-integrated annual estimates were 84% higher than the BU inventory, a difference driven almost entirely by compressor vents (rod packing and seal vents) and leakage through blowdown and isolation valves, which together accounted for 90% of the asset-level revision. The revision was heterogeneous across stations and source categories, emphasizing the importance of source-level, station-specific integration when developing an emissions inventory.</jats:p>
title:
Reconciliation
through Integration: A Source-Level
Bayesian Framework for Developing Measurement-Integrated Methane Inventories

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The effectiveness of shielding concrete in nuclear and medical facilities depends primarily on its density and radiation attenuation capacity. This study investigates the use of steel slag and direct reduced iron (DRI), two locally available industrial by-products, as heavyweight aggregates for enhancing gamma radiation shielding performance of concrete. An experimental program was conducted on concrete cube specimens and prismatic beams prepared with full replacement of conventional dolomite coarse aggregate and natural sand by slag-, iron powder-, and DRI-based aggregates. The main study variables were aggregate type and water-to-cement (w/c) ratio (0.40 and 0.50) resulting in a total of twelve mixtures. A conventional concrete mix containing dolomite and sand was used as the control specimen for comparison. The investigation included physical characterization (specific gravity and water absorption), mechanical testing (compressive and flexural strength), UPV measurements before and after irradiation, and gamma attenuation assessment through determination of the linear attenuation coefficient (LAC) and half-value layer (HVL). Concrete specimens with varying thicknesses were exposed to a Cesium-137 (Cs-137) gamma source emitting photons at 662 keV under narrow-beam transmission geometry. Results showed that heavyweight mixes incorporating slag and DRI achieved significantly higher LAC values and lower HVL compared to the control concrete. The best-performing mix exhibited an HVL of 2.09 cm, approximately 48% lower than the control mix, demonstrating superior shielding efficiency. This improvement was primarily attributed to the use of high-density slag and iron-based aggregates, which constituted the most influential variable governing radiation attenuation performance. Slag-based mixes also maintained or improved mechanical strength, while short-term irradiation (7 days) caused no significant internal integrity changes. These findings confirm that steel industry by-products can serve as sustainable and cost-effective alternatives to conventional heavyweight aggregates for structural gamma radiation shielding applications.</jats:p>
title: Enhancement of gamma radiation shielding performance of heavyweight concrete using slag and Direct Reduced Iron (DRI)

items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    At muon colliders, muon decays naturally produce intense electrons and positrons with unique features, namely high energies, high repetition rates, and small intrinsic uncertainties, that are unavailable at existing accelerator facilities. We quantitatively study the feasibility of extracting such particles in two representative future muon collider designs, IMCC and
                    <a:math xmlns:a="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <a:mi>μ</a:mi>
                      <a:mi>TRISTAN</a:mi>
                    </a:math>
                    . Using Monte Carlo simulations with the corresponding design parameters, we study the spatial, angular, and energy distributions of decay electrons and positrons in the curved sections of the collider ring. We find that typical deflections of 0.1–10 mrad can be achieved even for high-energy electrons carrying large energy fractions (
                    <c:math xmlns:c="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <c:mrow>
                        <c:mo>≃</c:mo>
                        <c:mn>0.6</c:mn>
                        <c:mi>–</c:mi>
                        <c:mn>1.0</c:mn>
                      </c:mrow>
                    </c:math>
                    ) of the muon beam energy, with the ring bending magnets (or magnets providing an equivalent field) effectively serving as a “preseptum magnet” that partially deflects the beam before the main septum magnet, suggesting that the extraction scheme could be practically feasible. Exploiting the distinct beam properties of IMCC and
                    <e:math xmlns:e="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <e:mi>μ</e:mi>
                      <e:mi>TRISTAN</e:mi>
                    </e:math>
                    , we propose complementary search strategies—missing energy and momentum searches for dark matter at
                    <g:math xmlns:g="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <g:mi>μ</g:mi>
                      <g:mi>TRISTAN</g:mi>
                    </g:math>
                    and visible-decay searches for axionlike particles and light scalars at IMCC—which probe parameter space beyond the reach of current and other proposed experiments.
                  </jats:p>
title: Muon collider experiments as electron and positron beam sources: Case studies of new light-particle searches

items.abstract:
<ns4:p>
                    Background Building vacancy and underutilization in consolidated urban centralities are multidimensional conditions that cannot be adequately characterized through occupancy status alone. This study develops a multi-source and multi-scale framework for diagnosing these conditions in La Mariscal, Quito, Ecuador. Methods The framework integrated citizen perception, systematic building-level field assessment, spatial statistics, and unmanned aerial vehicle-based light detection and ranging (UAV-LiDAR) data. A citizen-perception survey (n = 531) examined safety, urban activity, deterioration, and underutilization. Field assessment comprised 753 observations, consolidated into 691 unique parcels for spatial analysis. Getis–Ord Gi* statistics identified spatial concentrations, while UAV-LiDAR-derived building vertical extent was compared across vacancy/underutilization spatial groups using non-parametric tests. Results Citizen perceptions revealed the coexistence of urban activity and underutilization, with the strongest association between perceived deterioration and underutilization (Spearman’s ρ = 0.540, p < 0.001). Field observations revealed heterogeneous conditions, and spatial analysis identified differentiated clusters rather than uniform patterns of decline. Cross-source analysis of 685 parcels showed substantial overlap in building vertical extent among vacancy/underutilization cold spots, non-significant areas, and hot spots. Although the overall difference was marginally significant (p = 0.047), its effect size was very small (ε
                    <ns4:sup>2</ns4:sup>
                     = 0.009), and hot spots did not differ significantly from the other groups. Conclusions Urban underutilization involves differentiated combinations of activity, physical deterioration, street interaction, urban image, and revitalization potential. Building vertical extent alone does not provide a distinctive morphological signature of concentrated vacancy or underutilization. The proposed framework integrates perception, field evidence, spatial patterns, and three-dimensional morphology to support urban-regeneration diagnosis and adaptive-reuse prioritization.
                  </ns4:p>
title: A multi-source and multi-scale framework for diagnosing building vacancy and underutilization by integrating neighborhood-wide perception, parcel-level field assessment, spatial statistics, and UAV-LiDAR-derived urban morphology.

items.abstract: <jats:p>Decision support in protected horticulture must reconcile protocols, operating experience and sensor records that differ in representation, applicability and reliability and often conflict. This study develops a multi-source framework that determines when a recommendation may be executed automatically and when it should be deferred for human review. Stage 1 annotates each knowledge item with its applicability scope, classifies scope relations as compatible, unknown or conflicting, and vetoes conflicting links. Stage 2 converts agent probabilities into belief assignments, aggregates pairwise evidence conflicts into a gating score, and uses it to decide whether to act or defer. On the 310-day greenhouse tomato record, with an assumed deferral price of d = 0.35, the conflict gate yielded an observed expected cost of 0.2565 per decision day, against 0.2742 for always acting with the validation-selected agent, while executing 45% of decisions automatically; the paired block-bootstrap interval included zero, so the reduction is preliminary. This price is a decision-theoretic parameter assumed for the analysis, not a measured greenhouse operating cost; the difference indicates neither a reduction in production cost nor an improvement in irrigation management. Combining applicability-aware normalization with conflict gating turns disagreement into an operational act-or-defer signal.</jats:p>
title: A Conflict-Gated Decision Framework for Daily Irrigation Adjustment Using Multi-Source Knowledge: A Retrospective Study in a Tomato Greenhouse

items.abstract: <jats:p>In this study, we investigated the performance of surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensors using three distinct plasmonic metals—silver (Ag), copper (Cu), and aluminum (Al)—along with a dielectric titanium dioxide (TiO2) layer of varying thicknesses (0–3 nm) and a Molybdenum Ditelluride (MoTe2) layer. The sensing performance of the proposed SPR sensor was optimized by varying the TiO2 thickness (0–3 nm) while maintaining a fixed MoTe2 layer. The optimized multilayer configuration exhibited enhanced RI sensing performance compared with the corresponding structures under the investigated conditions. Key metrics, including sensitivity (S), minimum reflectance (Rmin), full width at half maximum (FWHM), detection accuracy (DA), and figure of merit (FoM), were used to assess the sensor performance at two refractive indices (ns = 1.33 and 1.335). The findings show that adding a thin layer of TiO2 and MoTe2 improved the sensitivity for all metal configurations. Because of their narrow FWHM, Al-based sensors produce the sharpest resonance curves with the highest FoM (up to 102.89/RIU), whereas Ag-based sensors have the highest sensitivity, reaching up to 321.2°/RIU. Cu-based sensors provide performance that balances spectral resolution and sensitivity. Depending on the metal, the ideal TiO2 thickness varies, but 1–3 nm offers the best trade-off. These results show how to optimize an SPR sensor’s sensitivity by customizing metal–dielectric combinations. After suitable surface functionalization with selective recognition layers, the suggested multilayer SPR structure shows outstanding performance for bulk RI sensing and offers a promising platform for future biomolecular sensing applications.</jats:p>
title: Refractive Index-Based Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensor for Bulk Sensing

items.abstract: <jats:p>Bacterial cellulose (BC) and dialdehyde cellulose nanofibrils (DA-CNF) are both nanoscale fibrillar materials with high specific surface areas and abundant surface hydroxyl groups. These features enable intimate interfacial contact with the resin matrix and facilitate the formation of a dense physical network within the coating. Therefore, developing nanocellulose-modified finish foil holds considerable promise for functional decorative surface applications in wood-based panels, particularly in interior decoration and furniture manufacturing. To investigate the effects of nanocellulose incorporation on the physico-chemical properties of finish foil, nanocellulose was introduced as a reinforcing agent into the electron beam (EB)-curable coating formulation. BC at mass fractions of 0.5%, 1.5%, and 2.5%, as well as DA-CNF alone and in combination with the preservative DIB-3, were incorporated into a polyacrylate resin system. The resulting mixtures were applied onto base coating paper and subsequently cured via electron beam irradiation to obtain modified finish foil samples. The structures and properties were characterized using ultra-deep three-dimensional microscopy (UDM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), tensile testing, organic volatile compound (VOC) analysis and anti-mold tests. Results revealed that electron beam-cured acrylic coatings with different nanocellulose formulations possess intact surface structures free of large cracks or delamination, while subtle surface undulations and micro-wrinkles originate from uneven shrinkage during curing. FTIR analysis verifies the characteristic chemical structures of polyester acrylate in the electron beam-cured finish foil, and residual acrylate C=C signals indicate incomplete curing due to the immobilization of reactive species in the crosslinked network. Tensile strength increased from 41.49 N to 46.00 N as BC content rose from 0.5% to 2.5%. Higher nanocellulose content intensified thermal decomposition, while DIB-3 suppressed the maximum degradation rate and shifted the main peak to higher temperatures. BC-based coatings showed lower relative headspace responses than DA-CNF for polar VOCs release, particularly N,N-dimethylformamide, sample D (2.5% BC + 0.8% DIB–3) showed the lowest relative headspace response for this specific compound. In anti-mold tests, no evident mold spots appeared on any sample after 55 days of indirect contact. Under 27 days of direct contact, group O (the finish foil coating was formulated without the addition of nanocellulose and preservative) remained virtually free of contamination, BC-containing groups were contaminated to varying degrees, while DA-CNF-based groups showed no obvious mold spread, suggesting that DA-CNF can prevent mold growth under the test conditions used. These findings provide a theoretical foundation and process reference for the development of functionalized EB-cured finish foil.</jats:p>
title: Investigation of the Performance of Nanocellulose-Modified Electron Beam-Curable Finish Foil

items.abstract: <jats:p>Copper chip/substrate interconnect is a promising replacement for conventional solder due to copper’s superior electrical, thermal, and mechanical performance. In this study, a chemically assisted method for thermomechanical sintering of copper microparticles at temperatures <200 °C is reported (i.e., low-temperature sintering). Formic acid pretreatment and the incorporation of an aromatic aldehyde, o-phthalaldehyde (oPA), provided a strong local reducing environment to fuse copper microparticles into a solid fillet in ambient air. Design-of-experiment (DOE) analysis was used to optimize the mechanical strength of the sintered part with respect to bonding time, aldehyde content, temperature, and applied pressure. Under optimized conditions (50 wt% formic acid and 10 wt% oPA), strong Cu discs were obtained in 6 min at 180 °C and 20 MPa.</jats:p>
